translations.idiomatic: Volume CCXXI

sentences.zh: 【唐紀三十七】 起屠維大淵獻，盡上章困敦，凡二年。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 37] Beginning in tuwei dayuanxian, ending in shangzhang kundun, altogether two years.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records 37], from the year jihai through the year gengzi—two years in all.

sentences.zh: 肅宗文明武德大聖大宣孝皇帝下之上乾元二年（

translations.literal: The latter part of the reign of Emperor Suzong, Cultured and Martial, Greatly Sagely and Greatly Promulgating, Filially Pious—above, Qianyuan year 2 (
translations.idiomatic: The latter part of the reign of Emperor Suzong of Tang—Qianyuan year 2 (

sentences.zh: 己亥，公元七五九年）

translations.literal: jihai, AD 759)
translations.idiomatic: jihai, AD 759)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，己巳朔，史思明築壇於魏州城北，自稱大聖燕王；

translations.literal: Spring, first month, first day jisi, Shi Siming built an altar north of Wei Prefecture city and styled himself Great Sagely King of Yan;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first day of the first month, jisi, Shi Siming erected an altar north of Wei Prefecture city and proclaimed himself Great Sagely King of Yan;

sentences.zh: 以周摯為行軍司馬。

translations.literal: He appointed Zhou Zhi as expedition marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Zhou Zhi expedition marshal.

sentences.zh: 李光弼曰：「思明得魏州而按兵不進，此欲使我懈惰，而以精銳掩吾不備也。

translations.literal: Li Guangbi said: "Siming has taken Wei Prefecture yet holds his troops and does not advance—this is meant to make us slack, then strike our unpreparedness with picked troops.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi said, "Siming has seized Wei Prefecture yet keeps his army idle—he means to lull us into negligence, then fall on us unawares with elite troops.

sentences.zh: 請與朔方軍同逼魏城，求與之戰。

translations.literal: I ask to press Wei city together with the Shuofang army and seek battle with him.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that we press Wei city together with the Shuofang army and force him to fight.

sentences.zh: 彼懲嘉山之敗，必不敢輕出。

translations.literal: Chastened by defeat at Jiashan, he will surely not dare sally lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Chastened by his defeat at Jiashan, he will not dare come out lightly.

sentences.zh: 得曠日引久，則鄴城必拔矣。

translations.literal: If we can draw the days out long, Ye city will certainly be taken.
translations.idiomatic: If we can prolong the siege, Ye city will fall of itself.

sentences.zh: 慶緒已死，彼則無辭以用其眾也。」

translations.literal: When Qingxu is dead, he will have no plea by which to employ his host."
translations.idiomatic: Once Qingxu is dead, he will have no pretext for keeping his army in the field."

sentences.zh: 魚朝恩以為不可，乃止。

translations.literal: Yu Chao'en deemed it impossible, and the plan was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chao'en opposed the plan, and it was dropped.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，上祀九宮貴神，用王璵之言也。

translations.literal: On wuyin the emperor sacrificed to the Nine Palaces' noble spirits, following Wang Yu's counsel.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin the emperor sacrificed to the spirits of the Nine Palaces, acting on Wang Yu's advice.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，耕藉田。

translations.literal: On yimao he plowed the sacred field.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao he performed the spring plowing ceremony in the sacred field.

sentences.zh: 鎮西節度使李嗣業攻鄴城，為流矢所中，丙申，薨；

translations.literal: Zhenxi military commissioner Li Siye attacked Ye city, was struck by a stray arrow, and on bingshen died;
translations.idiomatic: Li Siye, military commissioner of Zhenxi, was besieging Ye city when a stray arrow struck him; on bingshen he died;

sentences.zh: 兵馬使荔非元禮代將其眾。

translations.literal: the army-and-horse commissioner Lifei Yuanli took command of his troops in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: army-and-horse commissioner Lifei Yuanli took command of his forces.

sentences.zh: 初，嗣業表段秀實為懷州長史，知留後事，時諸軍屯戍日久，財竭糧盡，秀實獨運芻粟，募兵市馬以奉鎮西行營，相繼於道。

translations.literal: Earlier, Siye had memorialized to appoint Duan Xiushi Huai Prefecture chief secretary with charge of rear affairs; at the time the various armies had been encamped long, wealth exhausted and grain gone—Xiushi alone transported fodder and grain, recruited troops and bought horses to supply the Zhenxi expeditionary camp, one train following another on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Siye had recommended Duan Xiushi as chief secretary of Huai Prefecture with authority over rear-area affairs. The allied armies had been encamped so long that funds and grain were exhausted; Xiushi alone kept moving fodder and grain, recruiting soldiers and buying horses to sustain the Zhenxi expeditionary camp, with supply trains following one after another on the roads.

sentences.zh: 二月，壬子，月食，既。

translations.literal: Second month, day renzi, a lunar eclipse—total.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on renzi, there was a total eclipse of the moon.

sentences.zh: 先是百官請加皇后尊號曰「輔聖」，上以問中書舍人李揆，對曰：「自古皇后無尊號，惟韋後有之，豈足為法！」

translations.literal: Earlier the hundred officials had asked to add the honorific title "Assistant Sage" for the empress; the emperor asked Zhongshu attendant Li Kui, who replied: "From antiquity empresses have had no honorific titles—only Empress Wei had one; how can that serve as precedent!"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the officials had petitioned to grant the empress the honorific "Assistant Sage." The emperor consulted Zhongshu attendant Li Kui, who replied, "Throughout history empresses have borne no such honorifics—only Empress Wei did. How can that be a precedent!"

sentences.zh: 上驚曰「庸人幾誤我！」

translations.literal: The emperor said in alarm, "Mediocrities nearly led me astray!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor exclaimed, "Mediocrities nearly misled me!"

sentences.zh: 會月食，事遂寢。

translations.literal: When the lunar eclipse occurred, the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The lunar eclipse came, and the proposal was quietly dropped.

sentences.zh: 後與李輔國相表裡，橫於禁中，干豫政事，請托無窮。

translations.literal: Later he acted in concert with Li Fuguo, domineering within the palace, interfering in government, with endless petitions and entreaties.
translations.idiomatic: Later he and Li Fuguo worked hand in glove, throwing their weight about inside the palace, meddling in state affairs, and fielding endless petitions and favors.

sentences.zh: 上頗不悅，而無如之何。

translations.literal: The emperor was quite displeased yet could do nothing about it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply displeased but powerless to curb them.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀等九節度使圍鄴城，築壘再重，穿塹三重，壅漳水灌之。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi and eight other military commissioners besieged Ye city, building double ramparts, digging triple ditches, and damming the Zhang River to flood it.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi and eight other military commissioners invested Ye city, throwing up double lines of ramparts and triple ditches and damming the Zhang River to flood the town.

sentences.zh: 城中井泉皆溢，構棧而居，自冬涉春，安慶緒堅守以待史思明，食盡，一鼠直錢四千，淘牆及馬矢以食馬。

translations.literal: Within the city wells and springs all overflowed; they built platforms to live on. From winter into spring An Qingxu held firm awaiting Shi Siming; food was gone—a rat cost four thousand cash; they scraped walls and used horse dung to feed the horses.
translations.idiomatic: Wells and springs inside the walls brimmed over, and the defenders lived on raised platforms. From winter into spring An Qingxu held out, waiting for Shi Siming. When food ran out, a single rat fetched four thousand cash; they scraped plaster from the walls and fed their horses on dung.

sentences.zh: 人皆以為克在朝夕，而諸軍既無統帥，進退無所稟；

translations.literal: People all thought capture was a matter of days, yet the various armies had no overall commander and advanced or retreated with no one to report to;
translations.idiomatic: Everyone expected the city to fall within days, yet the allied armies had no supreme commander, and no one could tell them when to advance or pull back;

sentences.zh: 城中人欲降者，礙水深，不得出。

translations.literal: those in the city who wished to surrender were blocked by deep water and could not get out.
translations.idiomatic: while defenders who wished to surrender were trapped by the floodwaters and could not escape.

sentences.zh: 城久不下，上下解體。

translations.literal: The city long untaken, high and low alike came apart.
translations.idiomatic: The siege dragged on without success, and morale collapsed throughout the army.

sentences.zh: 思明乃自魏州引兵趣鄴，使諸將去城各五十里為營，每營擊鼓三百面，遙脅之。

translations.literal: Siming then led troops from Wei Prefecture toward Ye, ordering his generals to camp fifty li from the city each, every camp beating three hundred drums to threaten from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Siming then marched from Wei Prefecture toward Ye and ordered his generals to encamp fifty li from the city; each camp beat three hundred drums to harry the besiegers from a distance.

sentences.zh: 又每營選精騎五百，日於城下抄掠，官軍出，即散歸其營；

translations.literal: Moreover each camp chose five hundred picked horsemen to raid daily below the walls; when government troops came out, they dispersed back to camp;
translations.idiomatic: Each camp also picked five hundred elite horsemen to raid below the walls every day; when imperial troops sallied forth, the raiders scattered back to their camps;

sentences.zh: 諸軍人馬牛車日有所失，樵采甚艱，晝備之則夜至，夜備之則晝至。

translations.literal: the various armies lost men, horses, oxen, and carts daily; gathering firewood was very hard—guard by day and they came by night, guard by night and they came by day.
translations.idiomatic: and the allied armies lost men, horses, cattle, and wagons daily. Foraging for firewood became perilous: guard by day and the raiders struck at night; guard at night and they struck by day.

sentences.zh: 時天下饑饉，轉餉者南自江、淮，西自並、汾，舟車相繼。

translations.literal: At the time famine gripped the realm; those transporting provisions came from the south via the Yangzi and Huai, from the west via Bing and Fen, boats and carts following in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Famine gripped the empire, and supply convoys streamed in from the Yangzi and Huai in the south and from Bing and Fen in the west, boats and wagons in endless succession.

sentences.zh: 思明多遣壯士竊官軍裝號，督趣運者，責其稽緩，妄殺戮人，運者駭懼；

translations.literal: Siming often sent stalwarts to steal government army insignia, supervise and urge the transport men, blame them for delay, and kill people at will—the transport men were terrified;
translations.idiomatic: Siming sent many strong men to steal imperial insignia, then pose as overseers hurrying the convoys along, accusing carriers of delay and killing at whim until the transport crews were terrified;

sentences.zh: 舟車所聚，則密縱火焚之；

translations.literal: where boats and carts gathered, they secretly set fires to burn them;
translations.idiomatic: wherever boats and wagons clustered, they secretly set fires;

sentences.zh: 往復聚散，自相辨識，而官軍邏捕不能察也。

translations.literal: coming and going, gathering and dispersing, they recognized one another, while government troops patrolled and could not detect them.
translations.idiomatic: moving in and out, gathering and dispersing, they knew one another by signs the imperial patrols could never catch.

sentences.zh: 由是諸軍乏食，人思自潰。

translations.literal: Hence the various armies lacked food and men thought of breaking up on their own.
translations.idiomatic: The allied armies ran short of food, and soldiers began to think of slipping away.

sentences.zh: 思明乃引大軍直抵城下，官軍與之刻日決戰。

translations.literal: Siming then led his main force straight to below the walls, and the government army fixed a day for decisive battle with him.
translations.idiomatic: Siming then brought his main army up to the walls, and the imperial forces agreed to meet him in battle on a set day.

sentences.zh: 三月，壬申，官軍步騎六十萬陳於安陽河北，思明自將精兵五萬敵之，諸軍望之，以為遊軍，未介意。

translations.literal: Third month, day renshen, the government army's six hundred thousand infantry and cavalry formed battle lines on the north bank of the Anyang River; Siming personally led fifty thousand picked troops to oppose them—the various armies looked on them and thought them a roaming detachment, and paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on renshen, six hundred thousand imperial infantry and cavalry drew up on the north bank of the Anyang River. Siming himself led fifty thousand picked troops against them; the allied commanders took them for a scouting party and paid little heed.

sentences.zh: 思明直前奮擊，李光弼、王思禮、許叔冀、魯炅先與之戰，殺傷相半；

translations.literal: Siming pressed straight forward and struck fiercely; Li Guangbi, Wang Silun, Xu Shuji, and Lu Hui fought him first—casualties were about even;
translations.idiomatic: Siming charged straight in. Li Guangbi, Wang Silun, Xu Shuji, and Lu Hui met him first; casualties ran about even on both sides;

sentences.zh: 魯炅中流矢。

translations.literal: Lu Hui was struck by a stray arrow.
translations.idiomatic: and Lu Hui was hit by a stray arrow.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀承其後，未及布陳，大風忽起，吹沙拔木，天地晝晦，咫尺不相辨。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi followed after them but before he could deploy his formation a great wind suddenly rose, blowing sand and uprooting trees; heaven and earth were dark as day; within a foot one could not tell friend from foe.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi came up behind them, but before he could form his line a sudden gale blew up, whipping sand and tearing trees from the ground until heaven and earth turned dark and men could not see a foot before them.

sentences.zh: 兩軍大驚，官軍潰而南，賊潰而北，棄甲仗輜重委積於路。

translations.literal: Both armies were greatly alarmed; the government army broke south, the rebels broke north, casting off armor, weapons, and baggage piled along the road.
translations.idiomatic: Both armies panicked. The imperial forces broke south, the rebels north, leaving armor, weapons, and baggage heaped along the road.

sentences.zh: 子儀以朔方軍斷河陽橋保東京。

translations.literal: Ziyi used the Shuofang army to hold the Heyang bridge and protect the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi used the Shuofang army to hold the Heyang bridge and shield the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 戰馬萬匹，惟存三千，甲仗十萬，遺棄殆盡。

translations.literal: Of ten thousand battle horses only three thousand remained; of one hundred thousand suits of armor and weapons nearly all were abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Of ten thousand war horses only three thousand remained; of one hundred thousand sets of arms and armor nearly all were lost.

sentences.zh: 東京士民驚駭，散奔山谷，留守崔圓、河南尹蘇震等官吏南奔襄、鄧，諸節度各潰歸本鎮。

translations.literal: The people of the Eastern Capital were terrified and scattered into valleys; the acting commander Cui Yuan, Henan intendant Su Zhen, and other officials fled south to Xiang and Deng; each military commissioner broke up and returned to his own territory.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the Eastern Capital fled in terror into the hills. Acting commander Cui Yuan, Henan intendant Su Zhen, and other officials fled south toward Xiang and Deng, while the various military commissioners broke up and retreated to their home commands.

sentences.zh: 士卒所過剽掠，吏不能止，旬日方定。

translations.literal: Soldiers wherever they passed looted; officials could not stop them—it took ten days before order was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers plundered wherever they passed, and officials could not stop them; order was not restored for ten days.

sentences.zh: 惟李光弼、王思禮整勒部伍，全軍以歸。

translations.literal: Only Li Guangbi and Wang Silun tightened their ranks and brought their whole armies back.
translations.idiomatic: Only Li Guangbi and Wang Silun kept their units intact and brought their full armies home.

sentences.zh: 子儀至河陽，將謀城守。

translations.literal: Ziyi reached Heyang and was about to plan holding the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Ziyi reached Heyang he planned to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 師人相驚，又奔缺門。

translations.literal: The troops alarmed one another and again fled to Que Gate.
translations.idiomatic: His troops panicked one another and again fled toward Que Gate.

sentences.zh: 諸將繼至，眾及數萬，議捐東京，退保蒲、陝。

translations.literal: The generals arrived in succession; the host reached tens of thousands, and they debated abandoning the Eastern Capital and falling back to defend Pu and Shan.
translations.idiomatic: As the generals rejoined him his force swelled to tens of thousands, and some urged abandoning the Eastern Capital and falling back to defend Pu and Shan.

sentences.zh: 都虞候張用濟曰：「蒲、陝荐饑，不如守河陽，賊至，並力拒之。」

translations.literal: Chief adjutant Zhang Yongji said: "Pu and Shan suffer repeated famine—it is better to hold Heyang; when the rebels come, resist them with combined strength."
translations.idiomatic: Chief adjutant Zhang Yongji said, "Pu and Shan are repeatedly stricken by famine. Better to hold Heyang and meet the rebels with our combined strength when they come."

sentences.zh: 子儀從之。

translations.literal: Ziyi followed this counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi agreed.

sentences.zh: 使都游弈使靈武韓游瑰將五百騎前趣河陽，用濟以步卒五千繼之。

translations.literal: He sent roaming-inspection commissioner Han Yougui of Lingwu with five hundred horsemen ahead to Heyang; Yongji followed with five thousand foot.
translations.idiomatic: He sent roaming-inspection commissioner Han Yougui of Lingwu ahead with five hundred horsemen, and Yongji followed with five thousand infantry.

sentences.zh: 周摯引兵爭河陽，後至，不得入而去。

translations.literal: Zhou Zhi led troops to contest Heyang but arrived late, could not enter, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zhi raced for Heyang but arrived too late to enter and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 用濟役所部兵築南、北兩城而守之。

translations.literal: Yongji put his troops to work building south and north cities to hold them.
translations.idiomatic: Yongji set his men to building and holding twin cities on the south and north banks.

sentences.zh: 段秀實帥將士妻子及公私輜重自野戍渡河，待命於河清之南岸，荔非元禮至而軍焉。

translations.literal: Duan Xiushi led officers, soldiers, wives and children, and public and private baggage across the river from Yegu, awaiting orders on the south bank of Heqing; when Lifei Yuanli arrived they encamped there.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Xiushi led officers, soldiers, families, and public and private baggage across from Yegu and waited on the south bank of Heqing; when Lifei Yuanli arrived they made camp there.

sentences.zh: 諸將各上表請罪，上皆不問，惟削崔圓階封，貶蘇震為濟王府長史，削銀青階。

translations.literal: The generals each submitted memorials asking punishment; the emperor questioned none of them, only reducing Cui Yuan's rank and fief, demoting Su Zhen to chief secretary of the Prince of Ji's household, and stripping his silver-and-blue rank.
translations.idiomatic: The generals each submitted memorials asking to be punished; the emperor ignored them all, merely reducing Cui Yuan's rank and fief, demoting Su Zhen to chief secretary of the Prince of Ji's household, and stripping his silver-and-blue insignia.

sentences.zh: 史思明審知官軍潰去，自沙河收整士眾，還屯鄴城南。

translations.literal: Shi Siming, having ascertained that the government army had broken and gone, gathered and reorganized his troops from Shahe and returned to camp south of Ye city.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that the imperial army had broken and withdrawn, Shi Siming regrouped his troops at Shahe and encamped again south of Ye city.

sentences.zh: 安慶緒收子儀等營中糧，得六七萬石，與孫孝哲、崔乾祐謀閉門更拒思明。

translations.literal: An Qingxu gathered grain from Ziyi and the others' camps, obtaining sixty or seventy thousand piculs, and with Sun Xiaozhe and Cui Qianyou plotted to shut the gates and again resist Siming.
translations.idiomatic: An Qingxu gathered grain from the imperial camps—sixty or seventy thousand piculs—and with Sun Xiaozhe and Cui Qianyou plotted to shut the gates and resist Siming anew.

sentences.zh: 諸將曰：「今日豈可復背史王乎！」

translations.literal: The generals said: "Today how can we again turn our backs on King Shi!"
translations.idiomatic: His generals said, "How can we turn our backs on King Shi now!"

sentences.zh: 思明不與慶緒相聞，又不南追官軍，但日於軍中饗士。

translations.literal: Siming did not communicate with Qingxu, nor pursue the government army south, but daily feasted his troops in camp.
translations.idiomatic: Siming sent no word to Qingxu and did not pursue the imperial army south, but daily feasted his troops in camp.

sentences.zh: 張通儒、高尚等言於慶緒曰：「史王遠來，臣等皆應迎謝。」

translations.literal: Zhang Tongru, Gao Shang, and others said to Qingxu: "King Shi has come from afar—we all ought to go welcome and thank him."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tongru, Gao Shang, and others told Qingxu, "King Shi has come from far away—we ought all to go welcome him."

sentences.zh: 慶緒曰：「任公暫往。」

translations.literal: Qingxu said: "Lord Ren may go for the moment."
translations.idiomatic: Qingxu said, "Lord Ren may go for now."

sentences.zh: 思明見之涕泣，厚禮而歸之。

translations.literal: Siming saw him in tears, treated him with great courtesy, and sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: Siming received him in tears, treated him with great honor, and sent him back.

sentences.zh: 經三日，慶緒不至。

translations.literal: Three days passed and Qingxu did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Three days passed and Qingxu still did not come.

sentences.zh: 思明密召安太清令誘之，慶緒窘蹙，不知所為，乃遣太清上表稱臣于思明，請待解甲入城，奉上璽綬。

translations.literal: Siming secretly summoned An Taiqing to lure him; Qingxu, cornered and at a loss, then sent Taiqing to submit a memorial declaring himself Siming's subject, asking to wait until armor was laid aside to enter the city and present the imperial seal and cord.
translations.idiomatic: Siming secretly summoned An Taiqing to lure him in. Cornered and at a loss, Qingxu sent Taiqing with a memorial declaring himself Siming's subject, asking to lay aside arms and enter the city to present the imperial seal and cord.

sentences.zh: 思明省表，曰：「何至如此！」

translations.literal: Siming read the memorial and said: "Why go so far!"
translations.idiomatic: Siming read the memorial and said, "Why go so far!"

sentences.zh: 因出表遍示將士，咸稱萬歲。

translations.literal: He then produced the memorial and showed it throughout the army; all cried "Ten thousand years!"
translations.idiomatic: He then displayed the memorial to all his officers and men, who shouted "Long live the king!"

sentences.zh: 乃手疏唁慶緒而不稱臣，且曰：「願為兄弟之國，更作籓籬之援。

translations.literal: He then wrote in his own hand to condole with Qingxu without styling himself subject, saying moreover: "I wish us to be a nation of brothers and again be a fence of mutual aid.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote in his own hand to console Qingxu without calling himself a subject, adding, "Let us be brother realms and each other's bulwark again.

sentences.zh: 鼎足而立，猶或庶幾；

translations.literal: Standing like a tripod, we might yet hope for something;
translations.idiomatic: Standing three-legged like a tripod, we might yet prevail;

sentences.zh: 北面之禮，固不敢受。」

translations.literal: the rites of facing north I truly dare not accept."
translations.idiomatic: but I dare not accept the rites of a vassal facing north."

sentences.zh: 並封表還之。

translations.literal: He sealed and returned the memorial as well.
translations.idiomatic: He sealed Qingxu's memorial and returned it.

sentences.zh: 慶緒大悅，因請歃血同盟，思明許之。

translations.literal: Qingxu was greatly pleased and therefore asked to swear blood alliance; Siming agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Qingxu was delighted and asked to swear a blood oath of alliance; Siming agreed.

sentences.zh: 慶緒以三百騎詣思明營，思明令軍士擐甲執兵以待之，引慶緒及諸弟入至庭下。

translations.literal: Qingxu came to Siming's camp with three hundred horsemen; Siming ordered soldiers to don armor and take up weapons to await him, and led Qingxu and his brothers inside to the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Qingxu came to Siming's camp with three hundred horsemen. Siming had his soldiers arm and wait, then led Qingxu and his brothers into the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 慶緒再拜稽首曰：「臣不克荷負，棄失兩都，久陷重圍，不意大王以太上皇之故，遠垂救援，使臣應死復生，摩頂至踵，無以報德。」

translations.literal: Qingxu bowed twice and touched his forehead to the ground, saying: "Your subject could not bear the burden, lost the two capitals, long lay in heavy siege—never expecting that Your Majesty, for the Supreme Emperor's sake, would extend rescue from afar, making one who should have died live again; from crown to heel I have no way to repay such grace."
translations.idiomatic: Qingxu bowed to the ground and said, "Your subject failed in his charge, lost the two capitals, and lay long under siege. I never dreamed that you, for the Supreme Emperor's sake, would come so far to save me—one who should have died lives again. From crown to heel I cannot repay such grace."

sentences.zh: 思明忽震怒曰：「棄失兩都，亦何足言。

translations.literal: Siming suddenly flared in anger and said: "Losing the two capitals—is that worth speaking of?
translations.idiomatic: Siming suddenly blazed with anger. "Losing the two capitals—is that worth mentioning?

sentences.zh: 爾為人子，殺父奪其位，天地所不容！

translations.literal: You as a son killed your father and seized his place—heaven and earth will not bear it!
translations.idiomatic: You are a son who murdered his father and stole his throne—heaven and earth will not tolerate it!

sentences.zh: 吾為太上皇討賊，豈受爾佞媚乎！」

translations.literal: I am punishing the rebel for the Supreme Emperor—how should I accept your fawning flattery!"
translations.idiomatic: I have come to punish the rebel for the Supreme Emperor—why should I accept your fawning!"

sentences.zh: 即命左右牽出，並其四弟及高尚、孫孝哲、崔乾祐皆殺之；

translations.literal: He immediately ordered attendants to drag him out; together with his four younger brothers and Gao Shang, Sun Xiaozhe, and Cui Qianyou—all were killed;
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his attendants to drag Qingxu out; together with his four younger brothers, Gao Shang, Sun Xiaozhe, and Cui Qianyou, they were all put to death;

sentences.zh: 張通儒、李庭望等悉授以官。

translations.literal: Zhang Tongru, Li Tingwang, and the rest were all given offices.
translations.idiomatic: while Zhang Tongru, Li Tingwang, and the rest were all given offices.

sentences.zh: 思明勒兵入鄴城，收其士馬，以府庫賞將士，慶緒先所有州、縣及兵皆歸于思明。

translations.literal: Siming led troops into Ye city, gathered its soldiers and horses, used the treasury to reward officers and men, and all prefectures, counties, and troops formerly Qingxu's came under Siming.
translations.idiomatic: Siming marched into Ye city, took over its troops and horses, rewarded his soldiers from the treasury, and all the prefectures, counties, and armies that had belonged to Qingxu passed to Siming.

sentences.zh: 遣安太清將兵五千取懷州，因留鎮之。

translations.literal: He sent An Taiqing with five thousand troops to take Huai Prefecture and left him to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: He sent An Taiqing with five thousand men to take Huai Prefecture and left him to garrison it.

sentences.zh: 思明欲遂西略，慮根本未固，乃留其子朝義守相州，引兵還范陽。

translations.literal: Siming wished to press west at once but feared his base was not yet firm; he therefore left his son Chaoyi to hold Xiang Prefecture and led troops back to Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Siming wished to push west at once but feared his base was not secure; he left his son Chaoyi to hold Xiang Prefecture and marched back to Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 甲申，回紇骨啜特勒、帝德等十五人自相州奔還西京，上宴之於紫宸殿，賞賜有差。

translations.literal: On jiashen, fifteen men of the Uyghurs—Bonechuo tekle, Dide, and others—fled from Xiang Prefecture back to the Western Capital; the emperor feasted them in Zichen Hall and rewarded them in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, fifteen Uyghurs including Bonechuo tekle and Dide fled from Xiang Prefecture back to the Western Capital. The emperor feasted them in Zichen Hall and gave rewards according to rank.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，骨啜特勒等辭還行營。

translations.literal: On gengyin, Bonechuo tekle and the others took leave to return to the expeditionary camp.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin Bonechuo tekle and the others took their leave to return to the expeditionary camp.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，以荔非元禮為懷州刺史，權知鎮西、北庭行營節度使。

translations.literal: On xinmao, Lifei Yuanli was made prefect of Huai and acting military commissioner of the Zhenxi and Beiting expeditionary camps.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao Lifei Yuanli was appointed prefect of Huai and acting military commissioner of the Zhenxi and Beiting expeditionary camps.

sentences.zh: 元禮復以段秀實為節度判官。

translations.literal: Yuanli again appointed Duan Xiushi expeditionary adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanli again appointed Duan Xiushi his expeditionary adjutant.

sentences.zh: 甲午，以兵部侍郎呂諲同平章事，乙未，以中書侍郎、同平章事苗晉卿為太子太傅，王璵為刑部尚書，皆罷政事。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Vice Minister of War Lü Yin was made Fellow of the Secretariat; on yiwei, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Fellow Miao Jinqing was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, Wang Yu Minister of Justice—all removed from government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu Vice Minister of War Lü Yin was made Grand Councillor; on yiwei Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councillor Miao Jinqing was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Wang Yu Minister of Justice—all were removed from active government.

sentences.zh: 以京兆尹李峴行吏部尚書，中書舍人兼禮部侍郎李揆為中書侍郎，及戶部侍郎第五琦並同平章事。

translations.literal: Jingzhao intendant Li Xian was made acting Minister of Personnel; Zhongshu attendant and Vice Minister of Rites Li Kui Vice Director of the Secretariat; and Vice Minister of Revenue Diwu Qi—all Fellows of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhao intendant Li Xian was made acting Minister of Personnel; Zhongshu attendant and Vice Minister of Rites Li Kui Vice Director of the Secretariat; and Vice Minister of Revenue Diwu Qi—all were made Grand Councillors.

sentences.zh: 上於峴恩意尤厚，峴亦以經濟為己任，軍國大事多獨決於峴。

translations.literal: The emperor's favor toward Xian was especially deep; Xian also took statecraft as his own charge, and many great matters of army and state were decided by Xian alone.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor favored Xian above all; Xian took statecraft as his personal charge, and many military and civil decisions were made by him alone.

sentences.zh: 於是京師多盜，李輔國請選羽林騎士五百以備巡邏。

translations.literal: At this time the capital had many thieves; Li Fuguo asked to select five hundred Imperial Guard horsemen for patrol duty.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was plagued by thieves, and Li Fuguo asked to select five hundred Imperial Guard horsemen for patrol duty.

sentences.zh: 李揆上疏曰：「昔西漢以南北軍相制，故周勃因南軍入北軍，遂安劉氏。

translations.literal: Li Kui submitted a memorial saying: "Formerly the Western Han used the Southern and Northern armies to check each other; hence Zhou Bo entered the Northern Army through the Southern Army and thus secured the Liu house.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kui submitted a memorial: "In the Western Han the Southern and Northern armies checked each other; that was how Zhou Bo entered the Northern Army through the Southern and secured the Liu house.

sentences.zh: 皇朝置南、北牙，文武區分，以相伺察。

translations.literal: Our dynasty placed Southern and Northern guards, civil and military divided, to watch one another.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty placed Southern and Northern guards, civil and military kept apart, to watch one another.

sentences.zh: 今以羽林代金吾警夜，忽有非常之變，將何以制之！」

translations.literal: Now to use the Imperial Guard in place of the Golden Crow for night watch—if sudden extraordinary change occurs, how will it be controlled!"
translations.idiomatic: If the Imperial Guard replaces the Golden Crow for night watch, and sudden crisis strikes, how will we control it!"

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: The plan was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 丙申，以郭子儀為東畿、山東、河東諸道元帥，權知東京留守。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Guo Ziyi was made supreme commander of the Eastern Capital circuit, Shandong, and Hedong circuits, with acting charge of Eastern Capital garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen Guo Ziyi was made supreme commander of the Eastern Capital, Shandong, and Hedong circuits and acting garrison commander of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 以河西節度使來瑱行陝州刺史，充陝、虢、華州節度使。

translations.literal: Hexi military commissioner Lai Tian was made acting prefect of Shan and military commissioner of Shan, Guo, and Hua prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Hexi military commissioner Lai Tian was made acting prefect of Shan and military commissioner of Shan, Guo, and Hua.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，庚子，澤潞節度使王思禮破史思明將楊旻於潞城東。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day gengzi, Zelu military commissioner Wang Silun defeated Shi Siming's general Yang Min east of Lu city.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on gengzi, Zelu military commissioner Wang Silun defeated Shi Siming's general Yang Min east of Lu city.

sentences.zh: 太子詹事李輔國，自上在靈武，判元帥行軍司馬事，侍直帷幄，宣傳詔命，四方文奏，寶印符契，晨夕軍號，一以委之，乃還京師，專掌禁兵，常居內宅，制敕必經輔國押署，然後施行，宰相百司非時奏事，皆因輔國關白、承旨。

translations.literal: Crown Prince household head Li Fuguo, from when the emperor was at Lingwu, had held the post of acting expedition marshal of the supreme commander; he attended within the curtains, proclaimed edicts, and all documents from the four quarters, imperial seals and tallies, morning and evening army signals—everything was entrusted to him. On returning to the capital he took sole charge of the palace guard, constantly dwelling in the inner residence; all edicts had to pass Fuguo's countersignature before they could be carried out; the chief minister and the hundred offices, when presenting business out of hours, all went through Fuguo for notification and assent.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fuguo, household head of the Crown Prince, had served as acting expedition marshal from the time the emperor was at Lingwu. He attended within the imperial curtains, proclaimed edicts, and handled every document from the realm, every seal and tally, every morning and evening army signal. Back in the capital he took sole charge of the palace guard and lived in the inner quarters. No edict could be executed without his countersignature; the chief minister and every office that needed to report after hours had to go through Fuguo for clearance and assent.

sentences.zh: 常於銀台門決天下事，事無大小，輔國口為制敕，寫付外施行，事畢聞奏。

translations.literal: He often decided the affairs of the realm at the Yintai Gate; matters great or small—Fuguo spoke edicts by mouth, they were written and sent out to be carried out, and when done he reported to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He routinely decided affairs of state at the Yintai Gate. Great or small, Fuguo dictated edicts that were written down and sent out for execution, then reported to the throne when done.

sentences.zh: 又置察事數十人，潛令於人間聽察細事，即行推按；

translations.literal: He also set up several dozen investigators, secretly ordering them to listen in society for minute matters and immediately pursue and examine them;
translations.idiomatic: He also placed several dozen investigators in the field to eavesdrop on petty affairs and pursue them at once;

sentences.zh: 有所追索，諸司無敢拒者。

translations.literal: when there was pursuit and seizure, no office dared refuse.
translations.idiomatic: and when they pursued a case, no office dared refuse them.

sentences.zh: 御史台、大理寺重囚，或推斷未畢，輔國追詣銀台，一時縱之。

translations.literal: Heavy prisoners of the Censorate and Court of Judicial Review, even when investigation was not finished, Fuguo would summon to Yintai and release them all at once.
translations.idiomatic: Even serious prisoners held by the Censorate and the Court of Judicial Review, with trials still unfinished, Fuguo would summon to Yintai and release in a single stroke.

sentences.zh: 三司、府、縣鞫獄，皆先詣輔國咨稟，輕重隨意，稱制敕行之，莫敢違者。

translations.literal: The Three Offices, prefectures, and counties in trying cases all first went to Fuguo for consultation and report; severity or leniency as he pleased, styled as edict and carried out—none dared disobey.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Offices and every prefecture and county consulted Fuguo before trying a case, fixing punishment as he pleased under the label of imperial edict; none dared disobey.

sentences.zh: 宦官不敢斥其官，皆謂之五郎。

translations.literal: Eunuchs did not dare call him by his office; all called him Fifth Lord.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs did not dare use his title; all called him Fifth Lord.

sentences.zh: 李揆山東甲族，見輔國執子弟禮，謂之五父。

translations.literal: Li Kui of a great Shandong clan, on seeing Fuguo performed the rites due a younger kinsman and called him Fifth Father.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kui, scion of a great Shandong clan, treated Fuguo with the deference due a kinsman and called him Fifth Father.

sentences.zh: 及李峴為相，於上前叩頭，論制敕皆應由中書出，具陳輔國專權亂政之狀，上感寤，賞其正直；

translations.literal: When Li Xian became chief minister, he kowtowed before the emperor and argued that all edicts should issue from the Secretariat, fully setting forth Fuguo's monopoly of power and disorder of government; the emperor was moved to understanding and rewarded his integrity;
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xian became chief minister he kowtowed before the emperor and argued that edicts must come from the Secretariat, detailing Fuguo's abuse of power. The emperor was moved and praised his integrity;

sentences.zh: 輔國所行事，多所變更，罷其察事。

translations.literal: much of what Fuguo had done was changed, and his investigators were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: much of what Fuguo had done was reversed, and his investigators were abolished.

sentences.zh: 輔國由是讓行軍司馬，請歸本官，上不許。

translations.literal: Fuguo therefore yielded the expedition marshal post and asked to return to his original office; the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo then resigned as expedition marshal and asked to return to his original post; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，制：「比緣軍國務殷，或宣口敕處分。

translations.literal: On renyin, an edict: "Recently because military and state affairs were pressing, oral edicts were sometimes proclaimed for disposition.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin an edict declared: "Because military and civil affairs have been pressing, oral edicts have sometimes been used for disposition.

sentences.zh: 諸色取索及杖配囚徒，自今一切並停。

translations.literal: All sorts of requisitions and flogging assignments of convicts—from now all are stopped together.
translations.idiomatic: All requisitions and assignments of convicts to flogging are hereby stopped.

sentences.zh: 如非正宣，並不得行。

translations.literal: If not a proper proclamation, none may be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing not properly proclaimed may be carried out.

sentences.zh: 中外諸務，各歸有司。

translations.literal: All affairs within and without each return to the proper offices.
translations.idiomatic: All affairs within and without the court shall return to the proper offices.

sentences.zh: 英武軍虞候及六軍諸使、諸司等，比來或因論競，懸自追攝，自今一切須經台、府。

translations.literal: Adjutants of the Valiant Martial Army and envoys of the Six Armies and various offices—lately because of disputes they have on their own pursued and seized; from now all must go through the Censorate and prefectural offices.
translations.idiomatic: Adjutants of the Valiant Martial Army, envoys of the Six Armies, and all offices that have lately pursued and seized people on their own because of disputes must hereafter act only through the Censorate and prefectural authorities.

sentences.zh: 如所由處斷不平，聽具狀奏聞。

translations.literal: If the office handling the case decides unfairly, they may submit a detailed memorial to report.
translations.idiomatic: If the deciding office is unfair, the parties may submit a memorial to the throne.

sentences.zh: 諸律令除十惡、殺人、奸、盜、造偽外，餘煩冗一切刪除，仍委中書、門下與法官詳定聞奏。」

translations.literal: Of all statutes and ordinances, except the ten abominations, murder, adultery, theft, and counterfeiting, all the rest that are vexatious and redundant are entirely deleted, and the Secretariat, Chancellery, and legal officers are entrusted to examine and fix in detail and report."
translations.idiomatic: Of all statutes except the ten abominations, murder, adultery, theft, and counterfeiting, all redundant provisions are deleted, and the Secretariat, Chancellery, and legal officers are to revise the remainder and report."

sentences.zh: 輔國由是忌峴。

translations.literal: Fuguo therefore resented Xian.
translations.idiomatic: From this Fuguo came to hate Xian.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，置陳、鄭、亳節度使，以鄧州刺史魯炅為之；

translations.literal: On jiachen, the Chen, Zheng, and Bo military commission was established, with Deng Prefecture prefect Lu Hui appointed to it;
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen the Chen, Zheng, and Bo military commission was established, with Deng Prefecture prefect Lu Hui as commissioner;

sentences.zh: 以徐州刺史尚衡為青、密等七州節度使；

translations.literal: Xuzhou prefect Shang Heng was made military commissioner of Qing, Mi, and six other prefectures;
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou prefect Shang Heng was made military commissioner of Qing, Mi, and six other prefectures;

sentences.zh: 以興平軍節度使李奐兼豫、許、汝三州節度使；

translations.literal: Xingping Army military commissioner Li Huan was additionally made military commissioner of Yu, Xu, and Ru prefectures;
translations.idiomatic: Xingping Army military commissioner Li Huan was additionally made military commissioner of Yu, Xu, and Ru;

sentences.zh: 仍各於境上守捉防禦。

translations.literal: each still to guard and defend on his borders.
translations.idiomatic: each to guard and defend his own borders.

sentences.zh: 九節度之潰於相州也，魯炅所部兵剽掠尤甚，聞郭子儀退屯河上，李光弼還太原，炅慚懼，飲藥而死。

translations.literal: When the nine military commissioners broke at Xiang Prefecture, the troops under Lu Hui looted most severely; hearing Guo Ziyi had withdrawn to camp on the river and Li Guangbi returned to Taiyuan, Hui was ashamed and afraid and took poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the nine military commissioners broke at Xiang Prefecture, Lu Hui's troops had looted worst of all. Hearing that Guo Ziyi had withdrawn to the river and Li Guangbi to Taiyuan, Hui took poison in shame and fear.

sentences.zh: 史思明自稱大燕皇帝，改元順天，立其妻辛氏為皇后，子朝義為懷王，以周摯為相，李歸仁為將，改范陽為燕京，諸州為郡。

translations.literal: Shi Siming styled himself Great Yan emperor, changed the era name to Shuntian, made his wife the Lady Xin empress and his son Chaoyi Prince of Huai, appointed Zhou Zhi chancellor and Li Guiren general, changed Fanyang to Yan capital, and prefectures to commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Siming proclaimed himself emperor of Great Yan, adopted the era name Shuntian, made his wife Lady Xin empress and his son Chaoyi Prince of Huai, appointed Zhou Zhi chancellor and Li Guiren general, renamed Fanyang the Yan capital, and turned prefectures into commanderies.

sentences.zh: 戊申，以鴻臚卿李抱玉為鄭、陳、穎、亳節度使。

translations.literal: On wushen, Director of Guests Li Baoyu was made military commissioner of Zheng, Chen, Ying, and Bo.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen Director of Guests Li Baoyu was made military commissioner of Zheng, Chen, Ying, and Bo.

sentences.zh: 抱玉，安興貴之後也，為李光弼裨將，屢有戰功，自陳恥與安祿山同姓，故賜姓李氏。

translations.literal: Baoyu was a descendant of An Xinggui; he was Li Guangbi's lieutenant general and repeatedly had battle merit; he himself stated shame at sharing a surname with An Lushan, and therefore was granted the surname Li.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyu was a descendant of An Xinggui and served Li Guangbi as lieutenant general with repeated battle honors. He declared himself ashamed to share a surname with An Lushan and was granted the surname Li.

sentences.zh: 回紇毘伽闕可汗卒，長子葉護先遇殺，國人立其少子，是為登裡可汗。

translations.literal: The Uyghur qaghan Bögü Qaghan died; his eldest son Yabghu had been killed earlier; the people enthroned his younger son—this was Dengli Qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghur qaghan Bögü Qaghan died. His eldest son Yabghu had already been killed, and the people enthroned his younger son as Dengli Qaghan.

sentences.zh: 回紇欲以寧國公主為殉。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs wished to have Princess Ningguo follow him in death.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs wished to sacrifice Princess Ningguo to accompany the dead.

sentences.zh: 公主曰：「回紇慕中國之俗，故娶中國女為婦。

translations.literal: The princess said: "The Uyghurs admire Chinese custom, and therefore take Chinese women as wives.
translations.idiomatic: The princess said, "The Uyghurs admire Chinese custom—that is why they take Chinese wives.

sentences.zh: 若欲從其本俗，何必結婚萬里之外邪！」

translations.literal: If you wish to follow your native custom, why marry ten thousand li away!"
translations.idiomatic: If you wish to follow your native custom, why marry a woman from ten thousand li away!"

sentences.zh: 然亦為之剺面而哭。

translations.literal: Yet she also scarred her face for him and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Yet she scarred her face in mourning and wept for him.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔馬坊押官為劫，天興尉謝夷甫捕殺之。

translations.literal: A Fengxiang horse-pasture escort officer committed robbery; Tianxing magistrate Xie Yifu captured and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: A Fengxiang horse-pasture escort officer turned robber; Tianxing magistrate Xie Yifu captured and killed him.

sentences.zh: 其妻訟冤。

translations.literal: His wife sued claiming injustice.
translations.idiomatic: His wife sued, claiming injustice.

sentences.zh: 李輔國素出飛龍廄，敕監察御史孫鎣鞫之，無冤。

translations.literal: Li Fuguo had come from the Flying Dragon Stud; he ordered investigating censor Sun Jin to try the case—no injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fuguo, who had come from the Flying Dragon Stud, ordered investigating censor Sun Jin to try the case; Jin found no injustice.

sentences.zh: 又使御史中丞崔伯陽、刑部侍郎李曄、大理卿權獻鞫之，與鎣同。

translations.literal: He again had Vice Censor-in-Chief Cui Boyang, Vice Minister of Justice Li Ye, and Court of Judicial Review chief Quan Xian try it—with the same result as Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He had Vice Censor-in-Chief Cui Boyang, Vice Minister of Justice Li Ye, and Court of Judicial Review chief Quan Xian retry it; they agreed with Jin.

sentences.zh: 妻猶不服。

translations.literal: The wife still would not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: The wife still would not accept the verdict.

sentences.zh: 又使侍御史太平毛若虛鞫之。

translations.literal: He again had attendant censor Taiping Mao Ruoxu try it.
translations.idiomatic: He sent attendant censor Taiping Mao Ruoxu to try it again.

sentences.zh: 若虛傾巧士，希輔國意，歸罪夷甫。

translations.literal: Ruoxu was a crafty man who curried Fuguo's favor and laid guilt on Yifu.
translations.idiomatic: Ruoxu was a crafty man who curried Fuguo's favor and blamed Yifu.

sentences.zh: 伯陽怒，召若虛詰責，欲劾奏之。

translations.literal: Boyang was angry, summoned Ruoxu to rebuke him, and wished to impeach and memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: Boyang was furious, summoned Ruoxu to rebuke him, and prepared to impeach him.

sentences.zh: 若虛先自歸於上，上匿若虛於簾下。

translations.literal: Ruoxu first went to the emperor on his own; the emperor hid Ruoxu behind the curtain.
translations.idiomatic: Ruoxu went first to the emperor, who hid him behind the curtain.

sentences.zh: 伯陽尋至，言若虛附會中人，鞫獄不直。

translations.literal: Boyang soon arrived and said Ruoxu toadied to the inner attendants and tried cases unjustly.
translations.idiomatic: When Boyang arrived he said Ruoxu had curried favor with the eunuchs and judged unjustly.

sentences.zh: 上怒，叱出之。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and shouted him out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and had him driven out.

sentences.zh: 伯陽貶高要尉，獻貶桂陽尉，曄與鳳翔尹嚴向皆貶嶺下尉，鎣除名，長流播州。

translations.literal: Boyang was demoted to magistrate of Gaoyao, Xian to Guiyang, Ye and Fengxiang intendant Yan Xiang both to magistracies south of the ranges, Jin stripped of name and exiled far to Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Boyang was demoted to magistrate of Gaoyao, Xian to Guiyang, Ye and Fengxiang intendant Yan Xiang to posts in the Lingnan, Jin stripped of rank and exiled to Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書、同平章事李峴奏伯陽等無罪，責之太重；

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel and Fellow Li Xian memorialized that Boyang and the others were innocent and the punishment too heavy;
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel and Grand Councillor Li Xian memorialized that Boyang and the others were innocent and the punishments too severe;

sentences.zh: 上以為朋黨，五月，辛巳，貶峴蜀州刺史。

translations.literal: the emperor took it as faction; in the fifth month, day xinsi, Xian was demoted to prefect of Shuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor took it as factional defense. In the fifth month, on xinsi, Xian was demoted to prefect of Shuzhou.

sentences.zh: 右散騎常侍韓擇木入對，上謂之曰：「李峴欲專權，今貶蜀州，朕自覺用法太寬。」

translations.literal: Right Regular Attendant Han Zemu entered for audience; the emperor said to him: "Li Xian wished to monopolize power; now he is demoted to Shuzhou—I myself feel the law was applied too leniently."
translations.idiomatic: Right Regular Attendant Han Zemu came to audience. The emperor said, "Li Xian wanted to monopolize power; now that he is demoted to Shuzhou, I myself feel I was too lenient."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「李峴言直，非專權。

translations.literal: He replied: "Li Xian spoke straight—not monopolizing power.
translations.idiomatic: Zemu replied, "Li Xian spoke plainly; that was not monopolizing power.

sentences.zh: 陛下寬之，只益聖德耳。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty pardons him, it only adds to sagely virtue."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty pardons him, it will only add to Your sagely virtue."

sentences.zh: 若虛尋除御史中丞，威振朝廷。

translations.literal: Ruoxu was soon made Vice Censor-in-Chief; his authority shook the court.
translations.idiomatic: Ruoxu was soon made Vice Censor-in-Chief, and his authority dominated the court.

sentences.zh: 壬午，以滑、濮節度使許叔冀為汴州刺史，充滑、汴等七州節度使；

translations.literal: On renwu, Hua and Pu military commissioner Xu Shuji was made Bian Prefecture prefect and military commissioner of Hua, Bian, and five other prefectures;
translations.idiomatic: On renwu Hua and Pu military commissioner Xu Shuji was made prefect of Bian and military commissioner of Hua, Bian, and five other prefectures;

sentences.zh: 以試汝州刺史劉展為滑州刺史，充副使。

translations.literal: acting Ru Prefecture prefect Liu Zhan was made Hua Prefecture prefect and deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: acting Ru Prefecture prefect Liu Zhan was made prefect of Hua and deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 六月，丁巳，分朔方置邠、寧等九州節度使。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day dingsi, Shuofang was divided and Bin, Ning, and eight other prefectures given military commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on dingsi, Shuofang was divided and military commissioners were placed over Bin, Ning, and eight other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 觀軍容使魚朝恩惡郭子儀，因其敗，短之於上。

translations.literal: Army-oversight commissioner Yu Chao'en hated Guo Ziyi; because of his defeat he spoke ill of him to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Army-oversight commissioner Yu Chao'en hated Guo Ziyi and, using his defeat as pretext, slandered him to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，上召子儀還京師，以李光弼代為朔方節度使、兵馬元師。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, the emperor summoned Ziyi back to the capital and had Li Guangbi replace him as Shuofang military commissioner and army-and-horse supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, the emperor recalled Ziyi to the capital and replaced him with Li Guangbi as Shuofang military commissioner and supreme army commander.

sentences.zh: 士卒涕泣，遮中使請留子儀。

translations.literal: Soldiers wept, blocked the imperial envoy, and asked to keep Ziyi.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers wept, blocked the imperial envoy, and begged to keep Ziyi.

sentences.zh: 子儀紿之曰：「我餞中使耳，未行也。」

translations.literal: Ziyi deceived them, saying: "I am only seeing off the envoy—I am not leaving yet."
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi deceived them, saying, "I am only seeing off the envoy; I am not leaving yet."

sentences.zh: 因躍馬而去。

translations.literal: He then spurred his horse and left.
translations.idiomatic: Then he spurred his horse and rode away.

sentences.zh: 光弼願得親王為之副，辛巳，以趙王系為天下兵馬元帥，光弼副之，仍以光弼知諸節度行營。

translations.literal: Guangbi wished to have an imperial prince as his deputy; on xinsi the Prince of Zhao, Xi, was made supreme army-and-horse commander of the realm, with Guangbi as deputy, and Guangbi still held charge of the various military commissioners' expeditionary camps.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi asked for an imperial prince as deputy. On xinsi the Prince of Zhao, Xi, was made supreme commander of the realm's armies, with Guangbi as deputy, while Guangbi retained charge of the various expeditionary camps.

sentences.zh: 光弼以河東騎五百馳赴東都，夜，入其軍。

translations.literal: Guangbi with five hundred Hedong horsemen galloped to the Eastern Capital; at night he entered the army.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi galloped to the Eastern Capital with five hundred Hedong horsemen and entered the army by night.

sentences.zh: 光弼治軍嚴整，始至，號令一施，士卒、壁壘、旌旗、精彩皆變。

translations.literal: Guangbi governed the army with strict order; as soon as he arrived and a single order was issued, soldiers, ramparts, banners, and spirit all changed.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi ran a tight army. As soon as he arrived and his first orders went out, the troops, the camps, the banners, and the whole spirit of the force changed.

sentences.zh: 是時朔方將士樂子儀之寬，憚光弼之嚴。

translations.literal: At this time Shuofang officers and soldiers delighted in Ziyi's lenience and feared Guangbi's severity.
translations.idiomatic: The Shuofang troops had loved Ziyi's lenience and now feared Guangbi's severity.

sentences.zh: 左廂兵馬使張用濟屯河陽，光弼以檄召之。

translations.literal: Left wing army-and-horse commissioner Zhang Yongji was encamped at Heyang; Guangbi summoned him by dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: Left wing army-and-horse commissioner Zhang Yongji was encamped at Heyang; Guangbi summoned him by dispatch.

sentences.zh: 用濟曰：「朔方，非叛軍也，乘夜而入，何見疑之甚邪！」

translations.literal: Yongji said: "Shuofang is not rebel troops—entering by night, how great is the suspicion!"
translations.idiomatic: Yongji said, "Shuofang is not rebel territory—why enter by night with such suspicion!"

sentences.zh: 與諸將謀以精銳突入東京，逐光弼，請子儀；

translations.literal: He plotted with the generals to break into the Eastern Capital with picked troops, drive out Guangbi, and ask for Ziyi;
translations.idiomatic: He plotted with the generals to break into the Eastern Capital with elite troops, drive out Guangbi, and demand Ziyi's return;

sentences.zh: 命其士皆被甲上馬，銜枚以待。

translations.literal: he ordered his men all to don armor, mount horses, and hold gag-sticks in the mouth awaiting the word.
translations.idiomatic: he ordered his men to arm, mount, and wait in silence with gag-sticks in their mouths.

sentences.zh: 都知兵馬使僕固懷恩曰：「鄴城之潰，郭公先去，朝廷責帥，故罷其兵柄。

translations.literal: Chief army-and-horse commissioner Pugu Huai'en said: "At the Ye city rout Lord Guo left first; the court blamed the commander and therefore removed his military authority.
translations.idiomatic: Chief army-and-horse commissioner Pugu Huai'en said, "At the rout at Ye city Lord Guo withdrew first; the court blamed the commander and removed his command.

sentences.zh: 今逐李公而強請之，違拒朝命，是反也，其可乎！」

translations.literal: Now to drive out Lord Li and forcibly ask for him—defying and rejecting the court's order—is rebellion; how can it be done!"
translations.idiomatic: To drive out Lord Li and force them to recall Lord Guo would defy the court—that is rebellion. How can we do it!"

sentences.zh: 右武鋒使康元寶曰：「君以兵請郭公，朝廷必疑郭公諷君為之，是破其家也。

translations.literal: Right Martial Vanguard commissioner Kang Yuanbao said: "If you use troops to ask for Lord Guo, the court will surely suspect Lord Guo incited you—this destroys his household.
translations.idiomatic: Right Martial Vanguard commissioner Kang Yuanbao said, "If you use troops to demand Lord Guo, the court will suspect he incited you—that will destroy his household.

sentences.zh: 郭公百口何負於君乎！」

translations.literal: What has Lord Guo's hundred mouths done to wrong you!"
translations.idiomatic: What has Lord Guo's household done to wrong you!"

sentences.zh: 用濟乃止。

translations.literal: Yongji then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Yongji then abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 光弼以數千騎東出汜水，用濟單騎來謁。

translations.literal: Guangbi with several thousand horsemen went east out of Sishui; Yongji came alone on horseback to pay respects.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi rode east from Sishui with several thousand horsemen; Yongji came alone to pay his respects.

sentences.zh: 光弼責用濟召不時至，斬之，命部將辛京杲代領其眾。

translations.literal: Guangbi blamed Yongji for not coming when summoned in time, beheaded him, and ordered his subordinate general Xin Jinggao to take command of his troops in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi rebuked Yongji for failing to come promptly, beheaded him, and put his subordinate Xin Jinggao in command of his troops.

sentences.zh: 僕固懷恩繼至，光弼引坐，與語。

translations.literal: Pugu Huai'en arrived next; Guangbi led him to a seat and spoke with him.
translations.idiomatic: Pugu Huai'en arrived next; Guangbi seated him and spoke with him.

sentences.zh: 須臾，閽者曰：「蕃、渾五百騎至矣。」

translations.literal: Before long the gatekeeper said: "Five hundred Tibetan and Hun horsemen have arrived."
translations.idiomatic: Before long the gatekeeper announced, "Five hundred Tibetan and Hun horsemen have arrived."

sentences.zh: 光弼變色。

translations.literal: Guangbi's countenance changed.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi's face changed.

sentences.zh: 懷恩走出，召麾下將，陽責之曰：「語汝勿來，何得固違！」

translations.literal: Huai'en went out, summoned his subordinate generals, and feigned rebuke: "I told you not to come—how dare you stubbornly disobey!"
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en went out, summoned his officers, and feigned rebuke: "I told you not to come—why do you disobey!"

sentences.zh: 光弼曰：「士卒隨將，亦復何罪！」

translations.literal: Guangbi said: "Soldiers follow their general—what crime is theirs!"
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi said, "Soldiers follow their general—what crime is theirs!"

sentences.zh: 命給牛酒。

translations.literal: He ordered cattle and wine given them.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered cattle and wine given them.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，以潞沁節度使王思禮兼太原尹，充北京留守、河東節度使。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Luzhou and Qinzhou military commissioner Wang Silun was additionally made Taiyuan intendant and Northern Capital garrison commander and Hedong military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai Luzhou and Qinzhou military commissioner Wang Silun was additionally made Taiyuan intendant, Northern Capital garrison commander, and Hedong military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 初，潼關之敗，思禮馬中矢而斃，有騎卒盩厔張光晟下馬授之，問其姓名，不告而去。

translations.literal: Earlier, at the Tong Pass defeat, Silun's horse was struck by an arrow and died; a mounted soldier Zhang Guangcheng of Zhouzhi dismounted and gave him his horse, asked his name, and left without telling.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, at the defeat at Tong Pass, Silun's horse was killed by an arrow. A mounted soldier named Zhang Guangcheng of Zhouzhi dismounted and gave him his horse, asked his name, and left without giving his own.

sentences.zh: 思禮陰識其狀貌，求之不獲。

translations.literal: Silun secretly recognized his appearance and sought him but could not find him.
translations.idiomatic: Silun remembered his face and searched for him in vain.

sentences.zh: 及至河東，或譖代州刺史河西辛雲京，思禮怒之，雲京懼，不知所出。

translations.literal: When he reached Hedong, someone slandered Dai Prefecture prefect Hexi Xin Yunjing; Silun was angry at him, and Yunjing was afraid and knew no way out.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Hedong, someone slandered Dai Prefecture prefect Xin Yunjing of Hexi. Silun was angry, and Yunjing was terrified and at a loss.

sentences.zh: 光晟時在雲京麾下，曰：「光晟嘗有德於王公，從來不敢言者，恥以此取賞耳。

translations.literal: Guangcheng was then under Yunjing's command and said: "Guangcheng once had merit toward my lord; I have never dared speak of it, ashamed to gain reward thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Guangcheng was then in Yunjing's service and said, "I once did your lord a service at Tong Pass but never spoke of it, ashamed to claim a reward.

sentences.zh: 今使君有急，光晟請往見王公，必為使君解之。」

translations.literal: Now my lord is in peril; Guangcheng asks to go see my lord Wang—he will surely clear my lord."
translations.idiomatic: Now that my lord is in trouble, let me go to Lord Wang; he will surely clear you."

sentences.zh: 雲京喜，即遣之。

translations.literal: Yunjing was pleased and immediately sent him.
translations.idiomatic: Yunjing was delighted and sent him at once.

sentences.zh: 光晟謁思禮，未及言，思禮識之，曰：「噫！

translations.literal: Guangcheng paid respects to Silun; before he could speak Silun recognized him and said: "Ah!
translations.idiomatic: Guangcheng called on Silun. Before he could speak, Silun recognized him and cried, "Ah!

sentences.zh: 子非吾故人乎？

translations.literal: Are you not my old acquaintance?
translations.idiomatic: Are you not my old friend?

sentences.zh: 何相見之晚邪！」

translations.literal: Why meet so late!"
translations.idiomatic: Why did we meet so late!"

sentences.zh: 光晟以實告，思禮大喜，執其手，流涕曰：「吾之有今日，皆子力也，吾求子久矣。」

translations.literal: Guangcheng told the truth; Silun was greatly pleased, took his hand, and with tears said: "That I have today is all your strength; I have sought you long."
translations.idiomatic: Guangcheng told the whole story. Silun was overjoyed, took his hand, and wept: "What I am today is all your doing. I have searched for you so long."

sentences.zh: 引與同榻坐，約為兄弟。

translations.literal: He led him to sit on the same couch and pledged brotherhood.
translations.idiomatic: He drew him to sit on the same couch and pledged brotherhood.

sentences.zh: 光晟因從容言雲京之冤。

translations.literal: Guangcheng then at ease spoke of Yunjing's injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Guangcheng then spoke gently of Yunjing's injustice.

sentences.zh: 思禮曰：「雲京過亦不細，今日特為故人捨之。」

translations.literal: Silun said: "Yunjing's faults are not slight, but today I specially for an old friend let him go."
translations.idiomatic: Silun said, "Yunjing's faults are not slight, but today I forgive him for an old friend's sake."

sentences.zh: 即日擢光晟為兵馬使，贈金帛田宅甚厚。

translations.literal: That same day he promoted Guangcheng to army-and-horse commissioner and gave gold, silk, fields, and houses very generously.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he promoted Guangcheng to army-and-horse commissioner and gave him lavish gifts of gold, silk, fields, and houses.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，以朔方節度副使、殿中監僕固懷恩兼太常卿，進爵大寧郡王。

translations.literal: On xinmao, Shuofang military commissioner deputy and Palace Supervisor Pugu Huai'en was additionally made Director of Imperial Sacrifices and advanced in rank to Prince of Daning commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao Shuofang deputy military commissioner and Palace Supervisor Pugu Huai'en was additionally made Director of Imperial Sacrifices and advanced to Prince of Daning.

sentences.zh: 懷恩從郭子儀為前鋒，勇冠三軍，前後戰功居多，故賞之。

translations.literal: Huai'en had followed Guo Ziyi as vanguard, his courage leading the three armies; before and after his battle merit was greatest, and therefore he was rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en had served Guo Ziyi as vanguard with courage unmatched in the army and more battle honors than any other, and was rewarded accordingly.

sentences.zh: 八月，乙巳，襄州將康楚元、張嘉延據州作亂，刺史王政奔荊州。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day yisi, Xiang Prefecture generals Kang Chuyuan and Zhang Jiayan seized the prefecture and rebelled; prefect Wang Zheng fled to Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on yisi, Xiang Prefecture generals Kang Chuyuan and Zhang Jiayan seized the prefecture in revolt; prefect Wang Zheng fled to Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 楚元自稱南楚霸王。

translations.literal: Chuyuan styled himself Hegemon-King of Southern Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Chuyuan styled himself Hegemon-King of Southern Chu.

sentences.zh: 回紇以寧國公主無子，聽歸；

translations.literal: The Uyghurs, because Princess Ningguo had no son, permitted her return;
translations.idiomatic: Because Princess Ningguo had borne no son, the Uyghurs permitted her return;

sentences.zh: 丙辰，至京師。

translations.literal: on bingchen she reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: on bingchen she reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 戊午，上使將軍曹日昇往襄州慰諭康楚元，貶王政為饒州長史，以司農少卿張光奇為襄州刺史；

translations.literal: On wuwu the emperor sent General Cao Risheng to Xiang Prefecture to comfort and instruct Kang Chuyuan, demoted Wang Zheng to chief secretary of Raozhou, and made Vice Director of Agriculture Zhang Guangqi Xiang Prefecture prefect;
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu the emperor sent General Cao Risheng to Xiang Prefecture to reassure Kang Chuyuan, demoted Wang Zheng to chief secretary of Raozhou, and appointed Vice Director of Agriculture Zhang Guangqi prefect of Xiang;

sentences.zh: 楚元不從。

translations.literal: Chuyuan did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Chuyuan refused to comply.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，以李光弼為幽州長史、河北節度等使。

translations.literal: On renxu, Li Guangbi was made chief secretary of You Prefecture and Hebei military commissioner and related offices.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu Li Guangbi was appointed chief secretary of You Prefecture and Hebei military commissioner and related offices.

sentences.zh: 九月，甲午，張嘉延襲破荊州，荊南節度使杜鴻漸棄城走，澧、朗、郢、峽、歸等州官吏聞之，爭潛竄山谷。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on jiawu, Zhang Jiayan raided and broke Jing Prefecture; Jingnan military commissioner Du Hongjian abandoned the city and fled; officials of Li, Lang, Ying, Xia, Gui, and other prefectures, hearing this, all scrambled to flee secretly into mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on jiawu, Zhang Jiayan raided and captured Jing Prefecture. Jingnan military commissioner Du Hongjian abandoned the city and fled. When officials in Li, Lang, Ying, Xia, Gui, and other prefectures heard the news, they all scrambled to hide in the hills.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，更令絳州鑄乾元重寶大錢，加以重輪，一當五十；

translations.literal: On wuchen, the court again ordered Jiang Prefecture to cast Qianyuan Heavy Treasure large coins with an added double rim, each worth fifty;
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen the court again ordered Jiang Prefecture to cast Qianyuan Heavy Treasure large coins with a double rim, each to pass for fifty;

sentences.zh: 在京百官，先以軍旅畢無俸祿，宜以新錢給其冬料。

translations.literal: Officials at the capital, having earlier lost their salaries entirely because of military campaigns, were to be paid their winter rations in the new coin.
translations.idiomatic: Capital officials, who had already lost their salaries entirely to the war effort, were to receive their winter rations in the new coin.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，以太子少保崔光遠為荊、襄招討使，充山南東道處置兵馬都使；

translations.literal: On dinghai, Vice Grand Protector of the Heir Apparent Cui Guangyuan was made Jing and Xiang pacification commissioner and overall director of the Shannan East Circuit for disposition of troops and horses;
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai Vice Grand Protector of the Heir Apparent Cui Guangyuan was made Jing and Xiang pacification commissioner and overall director of troops and horses for the Shannan East Circuit;

sentences.zh: 以陳、穎、亳、申節度使王仲升為申、沔等五州節度使，知淮南西道行軍兵馬。

translations.literal: Chen, Ying, Bo, and Shen military commissioner Wang Zhongsheng was made military commissioner of Shen, Mian, and four other prefectures and given charge of Huainan West Circuit expeditionary troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Chen, Ying, Bo, and Shen military commissioner Wang Zhongsheng was made military commissioner of Shen, Mian, and four other prefectures and given charge of Huainan West Circuit expeditionary forces.

sentences.zh: 史思明使其子朝清守范陽，命諸郡太守各將兵三千從己向河南，分為四道，使其將令狐彰將兵五千自黎陽濟河取滑州，思明自濮陽，史朝義自白皋，周摯自胡良濟河，會於汴州。

translations.literal: Shi Siming had his son Chaoqing hold Fanyang and ordered each prefectural prefect to lead three thousand troops to follow him toward Henan, dividing into four routes: he had his general Linghu Zhang lead five thousand troops from Liyang to cross the river and take Hua Prefecture; Siming himself from Puyang, Shi Chaoyi from Baigao, and Zhou Zhi from Huliang to cross the river, meeting at Bian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Siming left his son Chaoqing to hold Fanyang and ordered each prefectural prefect to lead three thousand men south into Henan. He divided his force into four columns: his general Linghu Zhang was to take five thousand men from Liyang, cross the river, and seize Hua Prefecture; Siming himself would advance from Puyang, Shi Chaoyi from Baigao, and Zhou Zhi from Huliang, all crossing the river to rendezvous at Bian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 李光弼方巡河上諸營，聞之，還入汴州，謂汴滑節度使許叔冀曰：「大夫能守汴州十五日，我則將兵來救。」

translations.literal: Li Guangbi was just inspecting the camps along the river when he heard this; he returned to Bian Prefecture and said to Bian and Hua military commissioner Xu Shuji: "If you, sir, can hold Bian Prefecture for fifteen days, I will lead troops to rescue you."
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi was inspecting the camps along the river when he heard the news. He returned to Bian Prefecture and told Bian and Hua military commissioner Xu Shuji, "If you can hold Bian Prefecture for fifteen days, I will bring troops to relieve you."

sentences.zh: 叔冀許諾。

translations.literal: Shuji promised.
translations.idiomatic: Shuji agreed.

sentences.zh: 光弼還東京。

translations.literal: Guangbi returned to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi returned to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 思明至汴州，叔冀與戰，不勝，遂與濮州刺史董秦及其將梁浦、劉從諫、田神功等降之。

translations.literal: Siming reached Bian Prefecture; Shuji fought him but could not prevail, and so together with Pu Prefecture prefect Dong Qin and his generals Liang Pu, Liu Congjian, Tian Shegong, and others surrendered to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Siming reached Bian Prefecture, Shuji gave battle and was defeated. He then surrendered, along with Pu Prefecture prefect Dong Qin and his generals Liang Pu, Liu Congjian, Tian Shegong, and others.

sentences.zh: 思明以叔冀為中書令，與其將李詳守汴州；

translations.literal: Siming made Shuji Secretariat Director and had his general Li Xiang hold Bian Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Siming made Shuji Secretariat Director and left his general Li Xiang to hold Bian Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 厚待董秦，收其妻子，置長蘆為質；

translations.literal: he treated Dong Qin generously, took his wife and children into custody, and kept them at Changlu as hostages;
translations.idiomatic: he treated Dong Qin generously, took his wife and children hostage, and held them at Changlu as surety;

sentences.zh: 使其將南德信與梁浦、劉從諫、田神功等數十人徇江、淮。

translations.literal: he had his general Nan Dexin with Liang Pu, Liu Congjian, Tian Shegong, and several dozen others sweep the Yangzi and Huai regions.
translations.idiomatic: he sent his general Nan Dexin with Liang Pu, Liu Congjian, Tian Shegong, and several dozen others to sweep the Yangzi and Huai regions.

sentences.zh: 神功，南宮人也。

translations.literal: Shegong was a man of Nangong.
translations.idiomatic: Shegong was a native of Nangong.

sentences.zh: 思明以為平盧兵馬使。

translations.literal: Siming made him Pinglu army-and-horse commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Siming made him Pinglu army-and-horse commissioner.

sentences.zh: 頃之，神功襲德信，斬之。

translations.literal: Before long Shegong raided Dexin and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Shegong ambushed Dexin and killed him.

sentences.zh: 從諫脫身走。

translations.literal: Congjian escaped and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Congjian broke free and fled.

sentences.zh: 神功將其眾來降。

translations.literal: Shegong led his troops to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shegong brought his troops over to surrender.

sentences.zh: 思明乘勝西攻鄭州。

translations.literal: Siming pressed his victory and attacked Zheng Prefecture from the west.
translations.idiomatic: Siming pressed his advantage and marched west to attack Zheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 光弼整眾徐行，至洛陽，謂留守韋陟曰：「賊乘勝而來；

translations.literal: Guangbi reformed his troops and marched slowly; reaching Luoyang, he said to garrison commander Wei Zhi: "The rebels come riding their victory;
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi reformed his troops and marched slowly to Luoyang. He told garrison commander Wei Zhi, "The rebels are coming on the momentum of victory;

sentences.zh: 利在按兵，不利速戰。

translations.literal: the advantage lies in holding the army still; hasty battle is not to our benefit.
translations.idiomatic: our advantage lies in holding back; a quick fight would not serve us.

sentences.zh: 洛城不可守，於公計何如？」

translations.literal: Luoyang city cannot be held—what is your plan, sir?"
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang cannot be held. What do you propose?"

sentences.zh: 陟請留兵於陝，退守潼關，據險以挫其銳。

translations.literal: Zhi asked to leave troops at Shan, fall back to defend Tong Pass, and use the terrain to blunt their edge.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi proposed leaving troops at Shan, falling back to Tong Pass, and using the terrain to blunt the enemy's momentum.

sentences.zh: 光弼曰：「兩敵相當，貴進忌退，今無故棄五百里地，則賊勢益張矣。

translations.literal: Guangbi said: "When two foes are evenly matched, advance is prized and retreat is feared; now to abandon five hundred li of territory for no reason would only make the rebels' power swell all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi said, "When two equal foes meet, advance is prized and retreat is dangerous. To abandon five hundred li of ground for no reason would only swell the rebels' power.

sentences.zh: 不若移軍河陽，北連澤潞，利則進取，不利則退守，表裡相應，使賊不敢西侵，此猿臂之勢也。

translations.literal: Better to shift the army to Heyang, link north with Ze and Lu, advance when it profits and fall back to defend when it does not, with inner and outer positions answering each other, so the rebels dare not invade west—this is the 'ape's arm' posture."
translations.idiomatic: Better to shift the army to Heyang, link north with Ze and Lu, advance when we can and fall back when we must, with inner and outer positions supporting each other so the rebels dare not push west. That is the posture of an ape's arm.

sentences.zh: 夫辨朝廷之禮，光弼不如公；

translations.literal: In discerning court ritual, Guangbi is not the equal of you, sir;
translations.idiomatic: In matters of court ritual, Guangbi is no match for you;

sentences.zh: 論軍旅之事，公不如光弼。」

translations.literal: in discussing military affairs, you, sir, are not the equal of Guangbi."
translations.idiomatic: but in military affairs you are no match for Guangbi."

sentences.zh: 陟無以應。

translations.literal: Zhi had nothing with which to reply.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi had no reply.

sentences.zh: 判官韋損曰：「東京帝宅，侍中奈何不守？」

translations.literal: Adjutant Wei Sun said: "The Eastern Capital is the emperor's dwelling—how can the attendant-in-chief not hold it?"
translations.idiomatic: Adjutant Wei Sun said, "The Eastern Capital is the imperial residence—how can the attendant-in-chief abandon it?"

sentences.zh: 光弼曰：「守之，則汜水、崿嶺、龍門皆應置兵，子為兵馬判官，能守之乎？」

translations.literal: Guangbi said: "To hold it, troops must be posted at Sishui, Eling, and Longmen as well—you are army-and-horse adjutant; can you hold them?"
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi said, "To hold it we would have to garrison Sishui, Eling, and Longmen as well. You are army-and-horse adjutant—can you hold them?"

sentences.zh: 遂移牒留守韋陟使帥東京官屬西入關，牒河南尹李若幽使帥吏民出城避賊，空其城。

translations.literal: He then issued a dispatch ordering garrison commander Wei Zhi to lead Eastern Capital officials west through the passes, and a dispatch to Henan intendant Li Ruoyou to lead officials and people out of the city to avoid the rebels, emptying the city.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered garrison commander Wei Zhi by dispatch to lead Eastern Capital officials west through the passes, and Henan intendant Li Ruoyou to evacuate officials and civilians from the city, leaving it empty.

sentences.zh: 光弼帥軍士運油、鐵諸物詣河陽為守備，光弼以五百騎殿。

translations.literal: Guangbi led soldiers transporting oil, iron, and other supplies to Heyang for defense preparations; Guangbi with five hundred horsemen brought up the rear.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi led his soldiers in transporting oil, iron, and other supplies to Heyang to prepare its defenses, while he himself brought up the rear with five hundred horsemen.

sentences.zh: 時思明遊兵已至石橋，諸將請曰：「今自洛城而北乎，當石橋而進乎？」

translations.literal: At this time Siming's roaming troops had already reached Shiqiao; the generals asked: "Shall we now go north from Luoyang city, or advance at Shiqiao?"
translations.idiomatic: By then Siming's advance troops had reached Shiqiao. The generals asked, "Shall we go north from Luoyang, or advance through Shiqiao?"

sentences.zh: 光弼曰：「當石橋而進。」

translations.literal: Guangbi said: "Advance at Shiqiao."
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi said, "Advance through Shiqiao."

sentences.zh: 及日暮，光弼乘炬徐行，部曲堅重，賊引兵躡之，不敢逼。

translations.literal: At dusk Guangbi rode by torchlight and marched slowly; his ranks were solid and grave; the rebels led troops in pursuit but did not dare press close.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk Guangbi marched slowly by torchlight. His ranks held firm and steady, and though the rebels followed they did not dare close in.

sentences.zh: 光弼夜至河陽，有兵二萬，糧才支十日。

translations.literal: Guangbi reached Heyang by night; he had twenty thousand troops, and provisions enough for only ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi reached Heyang by night with twenty thousand troops and provisions for only ten days.

sentences.zh: 光弼按閱守備，部分士卒，無不嚴辦。

translations.literal: Guangbi inspected the defenses and assigned the soldiers; nothing was not strictly prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi inspected the defenses and assigned the troops; every detail was rigorously in order.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，思明入洛陽，城空，無所得，畏光弼掎其後，不敢入宮，退屯白馬寺南，築月城於河陽南以拒光弼。

translations.literal: On gengyin, Siming entered Luoyang; the city was empty and he gained nothing; fearing Guangbi would seize him from behind, he did not dare enter the palace, withdrew and encamped south of White Horse Temple, and built a crescent fort south of Heyang to oppose Guangbi.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin Siming entered Luoyang. The city was empty and he gained nothing. Fearing Guangbi might strike from behind, he did not dare enter the palace. He withdrew to camp south of White Horse Temple and built a crescent fort south of Heyang to block Guangbi.

sentences.zh: 於是鄭、滑等州相繼陷沒，韋陟、李若幽皆寓治於陝。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zheng, Hua, and other prefectures fell in succession; Wei Zhi and Li Ruoyou both administered from Shan in exile.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng, Hua, and other prefectures then fell one after another. Wei Zhi and Li Ruoyou both governed from Shan in exile.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丁酉，下制親征史思明；

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on dingyou, an edict was issued for the emperor to lead the campaign personally against Shi Siming;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on dingyou an edict was issued for the emperor to lead a personal campaign against Shi Siming;

sentences.zh: 群臣上表諫，乃止。

translations.literal: the ministers submitted memorials remonstrating, and the plan was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: the ministers submitted memorials urging him not to go, and the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 史思明引兵攻河陽，使驍將劉龍仙詣城下挑戰。

translations.literal: Shi Siming led troops to attack Heyang and had his fierce general Liu Longxian come to the foot of the wall to challenge battle.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Siming led troops against Heyang and sent his fierce general Liu Longxian to challenge the defenders below the wall.

sentences.zh: 龍仙恃勇，舉右足加馬鬣上，慢罵光弼。

translations.literal: Longxian relied on his bravery; he raised his right foot onto the horse's mane and insulted Guangbi with contempt.
translations.idiomatic: Longxian, trusting in his courage, rested his right foot on the horse's mane and hurled insults at Guangbi.

sentences.zh: 光弼顧諸將曰：「誰能取彼者？」

translations.literal: Guangbi looked at the generals and said: "Who can take that man?"
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi looked at his generals and asked, "Who can bring down that man?"

sentences.zh: 僕固懷恩請行。

translations.literal: Pugu Huai'en asked to go.
translations.idiomatic: Pugu Huai'en volunteered.
