sentences.zh: 光弼曰：「此非大將所為。」

translations.literal: Guangbi said: "This is not work for a chief general."
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi said, "This is not work for a chief general."

sentences.zh: 左右言「裨將白孝德可往。」

translations.literal: Those beside him said: "Lieutenant general Bai Xiaode can go."
translations.idiomatic: Those beside him said, "Lieutenant general Bai Xiaode can go."

sentences.zh: 光弼召問之。

translations.literal: Guangbi summoned and questioned him.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi summoned him and questioned him.

sentences.zh: 孝德請行。

translations.literal: Xiaode asked to go.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaode volunteered.

sentences.zh: 光弼問：「須幾何兵？」

translations.literal: Guangbi asked: "How many troops do you need?"
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi asked, "How many men do you need?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「請挺身取之。」

translations.literal: He replied: "I ask to go alone and take him."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I ask to go alone and take him."

sentences.zh: 光弼壯其志，然固問所須。

translations.literal: Guangbi admired his resolve, yet still pressed him on what he required.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi admired his spirit but still pressed him on what he needed.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「願選五十騎出壘門為後繼，兼請大軍助鼓噪以增氣。」

translations.literal: He replied: "I wish to choose fifty horsemen to sally from the camp gate as reinforcements, and also ask the main army to help with drum and shout to raise morale."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I want fifty horsemen to sally from the camp gate as backup, and I ask the main army to drum and shout to raise our spirits."

sentences.zh: 光弼撫其背而遣之。

translations.literal: Guangbi patted his back and sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi clapped him on the back and sent him off.

sentences.zh: 孝德挾二矛，策馬亂流而進。

translations.literal: Xiaode tucked two spears under his arms and spurred his horse through the swirling current to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaode tucked two spears under his arms and spurred his horse through the swirling current.

sentences.zh: 半涉，懷恩賀曰：「克矣。」

translations.literal: When he was halfway across, Huai'en congratulated him, saying: "He is taken."
translations.idiomatic: When he was halfway across, Huai'en cried, "He is as good as taken."

sentences.zh: 光弼曰：「鋒未交，何以知之？」

translations.literal: Guangbi said: "The points have not yet crossed—how do you know?"
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi said, "The blades have not yet crossed—how do you know?"

sentences.zh: 懷恩曰：「觀其攬轡安閒，知其萬全。」

translations.literal: Huai'en said: "Watching him hold the reins at ease, I know he is completely secure."
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en said, "Watch how calmly he holds the reins—I know he is completely sure of himself."

sentences.zh: 龍仙見其獨來，甚易之；

translations.literal: Longxian saw him come alone and thought him very easy prey;
translations.idiomatic: Longxian saw him come alone and took him lightly;

sentences.zh: 稍近，將動，孝德搖手示之，若非來為敵者，龍仙不測而止。

translations.literal: as he drew slightly nearer and was about to move, Xiaode waved his hand to show him, as if not coming as an enemy; Longxian, unable to fathom it, stopped.
translations.idiomatic: as he drew nearer and was about to move, Xiaode waved his hand as if he were not coming as an enemy. Longxian, unable to read him, held still.

sentences.zh: 去之十步，乃與之言，龍仙慢罵如初。

translations.literal: When ten paces remained between them, he spoke with him; Longxian insulted him with contempt as before.
translations.idiomatic: When they were ten paces apart, they spoke; Longxian hurled the same contemptuous insults as before.

sentences.zh: 孝德息馬良久，因瞋目謂曰：「賊識我乎？」

translations.literal: Xiaode rested his horse for a long while, then glared and said: "Rebel, do you know me?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiaode reined in his horse for a long while, then glared and said, "Rebel, do you know who I am?"

sentences.zh: 龍仙曰：「誰也？」

translations.literal: Longxian said: "Who are you?"
translations.idiomatic: Longxian said, "Who are you?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「我，白孝德也。」

translations.literal: He said: "I am Bai Xiaode."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "I am Bai Xiaode."

sentences.zh: 龍仙曰：「是何狗彘！」

translations.literal: Longxian said: "What kind of dog or swine is this!"
translations.idiomatic: Longxian said, "What kind of cur is this!"

sentences.zh: 孝德大呼，運矛躍馬搏之。

translations.literal: Xiaode shouted loudly, swung his spear, leaped his horse, and grappled with him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaode shouted, swung his spear, spurred his horse forward, and closed with him.

sentences.zh: 城上鼓噪，五十騎繼進。

translations.literal: On the wall drums and shouts rose; fifty horsemen followed in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Drums and shouts rose from the wall as fifty horsemen charged out in support.

sentences.zh: 龍仙矢不及發，環走堤上。

translations.literal: Longxian could not even release an arrow; he circled along the embankment.
translations.idiomatic: Longxian could not even get off a shot and circled along the embankment.

sentences.zh: 孝德追及，斬首，攜之以歸。

translations.literal: Xiaode overtook him, cut off his head, and carried it back.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaode caught him, cut off his head, and carried it back.

sentences.zh: 賊眾大駭。

translations.literal: The rebel host was greatly terrified.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel troops were terrified.

sentences.zh: 孝德，本安西胡人也。

translations.literal: Xiaode was originally a Hu man of Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaode was originally a Hu from Anxi.

sentences.zh: 思明有良馬千餘匹，每日出於河南渚浴之，循環不休以示多。

translations.literal: Siming had more than a thousand fine horses; each day they were brought out to bathe at the Henan sandbars, circulating without cease to display their numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Siming had more than a thousand fine horses. Each day they were brought out to bathe at the Henan sandbars, circling endlessly to show how many he had.

sentences.zh: 光弼命索軍中牝馬，得五百匹，縶其駒於城內。

translations.literal: Guangbi ordered a search for mares in the army; five hundred were found, and their foals were tethered inside the city.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi ordered a search for mares in the army and found five hundred. Their foals were tethered inside the city.

sentences.zh: 俟思明馬至水際，盡出之，馬嘶不已，思明馬悉浮渡河，一時驅之入城。

translations.literal: When Siming's horses reached the water's edge, all the mares were released; the horses neighed without cease; Siming's horses all swam across the river, and in one stroke they were driven into the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Siming's horses reached the water's edge, all the mares were released. They neighed without cease, Siming's horses swam across the river, and in one rush they were driven into the city.

sentences.zh: 思明怒，列戰船數百艘，泛火船於前而隨之，欲乘流燒浮橋。

translations.literal: Siming was enraged; he arrayed several hundred warships, floated fire ships in front and followed after them, intending to use the current to burn the pontoon bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Siming was furious. He lined up several hundred warships, sent fire ships ahead down the current, and followed them, hoping to burn the pontoon bridge.

sentences.zh: 光弼先貯百尺長竿數百枚，以巨木承其根，氈裹鐵叉置其首，以迎火船而叉之。

translations.literal: Guangbi had earlier stored several hundred hundred-foot-long poles; great timbers supported their roots, and felt-wrapped iron forks were set at their tips to meet the fire ships and fork them.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi had already stockpiled several hundred poles, each a hundred feet long mounted on great timbers, with felt-wrapped iron forks at the tips to meet the fire ships and hook them aside.

sentences.zh: 船不得進，須臾自焚盡。

translations.literal: The ships could not advance; in a moment they all burned out by themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The ships could not advance and in a moment burned out on their own.

sentences.zh: 又以叉拒戰船，於橋上發砲石擊之，中者皆沉沒，賊不勝而去。

translations.literal: They also used forks to repel the warships, and from the bridge launched catapult stones to strike them; those hit all sank, and the rebels could not prevail and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: They also used the forks to fend off the warships and hurled catapult stones from the bridge. Every ship struck sank, and the rebels withdrew defeated.

sentences.zh: 思明見兵於河清，欲絕光弼糧道，光弼軍於野水渡以備之。

translations.literal: Siming displayed troops at Heqing, intending to cut off Guangbi's supply route; Guangbi encamped at Yeshui Ford to guard against this.
translations.idiomatic: Siming showed troops at Heqing, intending to cut Guangbi's supply line. Guangbi encamped at Yeshui Ford to block him.

sentences.zh: 既夕，還河陽，留兵千人，使部將雍希顥守其柵，曰：「賊將高庭暉、李日越、喻文景，皆萬人敵也。

translations.literal: At evening he returned to Heyang, leaving a thousand troops and having his subordinate general Yong Xihao hold the palisade; he said: "The rebel generals Gao Tinghui, Li Riyue, and Yu Wenjing are each a match for ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: At evening he returned to Heyang, leaving a thousand men under his subordinate Yong Xihao to hold the palisade. He said, "The rebel generals Gao Tinghui, Li Riyue, and Yu Wenjing are each a match for ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 思明必使一人來劫我。

translations.literal: Siming will surely send one of them to raid us.
translations.idiomatic: Siming is sure to send one of them to raid us.

sentences.zh: 我且去之，汝待於此。

translations.literal: I shall leave for now; you wait here.
translations.idiomatic: I am leaving for now. You wait here.

sentences.zh: 若賊至，勿與之戰。

translations.literal: If the rebels come, do not fight them.
translations.idiomatic: If the rebels come, do not fight them.

sentences.zh: 降，則與之俱來。」

translations.literal: If they surrender, come back with them."
translations.idiomatic: If they surrender, bring them back with you."

sentences.zh: 諸將莫諭其意，皆竊笑之。

translations.literal: The generals none understood his meaning and all secretly laughed at him.
translations.idiomatic: None of the generals understood what he meant, and they all laughed behind his back.

sentences.zh: 既而思明果謂李日越曰：「李光弼長於憑城，今出在野，此成擒矣。

translations.literal: Before long Siming indeed said to Li Riyue: "Li Guangbi excels at fighting from walled positions; now he is out in the open—this is a sure capture.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Siming did say to Li Riyue, "Li Guangbi excels at fighting from behind walls. Now he is out in the open—this is a sure capture.

sentences.zh: 汝以鐵騎宵濟，為我取之，不得，則勿返。」

translations.literal: You with iron cavalry cross by night, take him for me; if you do not succeed, do not return."
translations.idiomatic: Take iron cavalry across by night and seize him for me. If you fail, do not come back."

sentences.zh: 日越將五百騎晨至柵下，希顥阻壕休卒，吟嘯相視。

translations.literal: Riyue with five hundred horsemen reached the palisade at dawn; Xihao blocked the moat and rested his soldiers, humming and whistling as they looked at one another.
translations.idiomatic: Riyue arrived at the palisade at dawn with five hundred horsemen. Xihao blocked the moat, rested his men, and hummed and whistled as they looked at one another.

sentences.zh: 日越怪之，問曰：「司空在乎？」

translations.literal: Riyue thought it strange and asked: "Is the Minister of Works here?"
translations.idiomatic: Riyue found it strange and asked, "Is the Minister of Works here?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「夜去矣。」

translations.literal: He was told: "He left last night."
translations.idiomatic: He was told, "He left last night."

sentences.zh: 「兵幾何？」

translations.literal: "How many troops?"
translations.idiomatic: "How many men?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「千人。」

translations.literal: He was told: "A thousand men."
translations.idiomatic: "A thousand."

sentences.zh: 「將誰？」

translations.literal: "Who is the commander?"
translations.idiomatic: "Who commands them?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「雍希顥。」

translations.literal: He was told: "Yong Xihao."
translations.idiomatic: "Yong Xihao."

sentences.zh: 日越默計久之，謂其下曰：「今失李光弼，得希顥而歸，吾死必矣，不如降也。」

translations.literal: Riyue calculated silently for a long while and said to his men: "Now having missed Li Guangbi and returning with only Xihao, I am sure to die—better to surrender."
translations.idiomatic: Riyue thought for a long while and then told his men, "I missed Li Guangbi and would return with only Xihao—I am as good as dead. Better to surrender."

sentences.zh: 遂請降。

translations.literal: He then asked to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He then offered to surrender.

sentences.zh: 希顥與之俱見光弼，光弼厚待之，任以心腹。

translations.literal: Xihao went with him together to see Guangbi; Guangbi treated him generously and entrusted him as a close confidant.
translations.idiomatic: Xihao brought him to Guangbi, who treated him generously and took him into his inner circle.

sentences.zh: 高庭暉聞之，亦降。

translations.literal: Gao Tinghui, hearing this, also surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Tinghui heard of it, he surrendered too.

sentences.zh: 或問光弼：「降二將何易也？」

translations.literal: Someone asked Guangbi: "How was getting two generals to surrender so easy?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked Li Guangbi, "Why was it so easy to get those two generals to defect?

sentences.zh: 光弼曰：「此人情耳。

translations.literal: Guangbi said: "This is simply human nature.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi replied, "That is simply human nature.

sentences.zh: 思明常恨不得野戰，聞我在外，以為必可取。

translations.literal: Siming has always longed for field battle; hearing that I was away, he thought I could surely be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Siming has always wished for a pitched battle in the open field. When he heard I was away from the city, he assumed I could be captured.

sentences.zh: 日越不獲我，勢不敢歸。

translations.literal: Riyue did not capture me; having failed, he would not dare return.
translations.idiomatic: Riyue failed to take me, so he would not dare go back empty-handed.

sentences.zh: 庭暉才勇過於日越，聞日越被寵任，必思奪之矣。」

translations.literal: Tinghui's talent and valor surpass Riyue's; hearing Riyue favored and entrusted, he would surely think to wrest it from him."
translations.idiomatic: Tinghui is more gifted and bold than Riyue. Once he heard Riyue had been favored and given command, he would be bound to try to supplant him.

sentences.zh: 庭暉時為五台府果毅。

translations.literal: At the time Tinghui was a guoyi of Wutai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Tinghui was then a guoyi officer of Wutai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 己亥，以庭暉為右武衛大將軍。

translations.literal: On jihai, Tinghui was made Grand General of the Right Martial Guard."
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, Gao Tinghui was appointed Grand General of the Right Martial Guard."

sentences.zh: 思明復攻河陽，光弼謂鄭陳節度使李抱玉曰：「將軍能為我守南城二日乎？」

translations.literal: Siming again attacked Heyang. Guangbi said to Zheng-Chen military governor Li Baoyu: "Can the general hold the south city for me two days?"
translations.idiomatic: Shi Siming again attacked Heyang. Li Guangbi said to Li Baoyu, military governor of Zheng and Chen, "Can you hold the south city for me for two days?

sentences.zh: 抱玉曰：「過期何如？」

translations.literal: Baoyu said: "If the deadline passes, then what?"
translations.idiomatic: Baoyu asked, "And if the two days pass?

sentences.zh: 光弼曰：「過期救不至，任棄之。」

translations.literal: Guangbi said: "If the deadline passes and relief does not arrive, you may abandon it at will."
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi said, "If the deadline passes and relief has not come, you may abandon the city.

sentences.zh: 抱玉許諾，勒兵拒守。

translations.literal: Baoyu assented and drew up his troops to resist and hold.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyu agreed and marshaled his troops to defend the walls.

sentences.zh: 城且陷，抱玉紿之曰：「吾糧盡，明旦當降。」

translations.literal: The city was on the point of falling; Baoyu deceived them, saying: "Our grain is exhausted; tomorrow morning we shall surrender."
translations.idiomatic: When the city was nearly lost, Baoyu deceived the enemy, saying, "Our provisions are spent. We will surrender tomorrow morning.

sentences.zh: 賊喜，斂軍以待之。

translations.literal: The rebels rejoiced, drew in their army, and waited.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels rejoiced, pulled back their forces, and waited.

sentences.zh: 抱玉繕完城備，明日，復請戰。

translations.literal: Baoyu repaired and completed the city's defenses; the next day he again asked to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyu used the respite to repair the defenses, and the next day he offered battle again.

sentences.zh: 賊怒，急攻之。

translations.literal: The rebels were enraged and pressed the attack fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the rebels pressed the assault.

sentences.zh: 抱玉出奇兵，表裡夾擊，殺傷甚眾。

translations.literal: Baoyu sent out surprise troops and struck from inside and out; killed and wounded were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyu sent out a surprise force and attacked from inside and out, inflicting heavy casualties.

sentences.zh: 董秦從思明寇河陽，夜帥其眾五百，拔柵突圍，降於光弼。

translations.literal: Dong Qin followed Siming in raiding Heyang; by night he led his five hundred men, pulled up the palisade and burst through the encirclement, and surrendered to Guangbi.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Qin had followed Shi Siming in the attack on Heyang. By night he led five hundred men, tore down the palisade, broke out of the encirclement, and surrendered to Li Guangbi.

sentences.zh: 時光弼自將屯中水單，城外置柵，柵外穿塹，深廣二丈。

translations.literal: At the time Guangbi personally commanded and encamped at Zhongshui camp; outside the city he set palisades, and outside the palisades dug a moat twenty chi deep and wide.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi was then in personal command at the Zhongshui encampment. Outside the city he had built palisades, and beyond them a moat twenty chi deep and wide.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，賊將周摯捨南城，並力攻中水單。

translations.literal: On yisi, the rebel general Zhou Zhi abandoned the south city and combined forces to attack Zhongshui camp.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi the rebel general Zhou Zhi gave up the south city and concentrated his forces against the Zhongshui encampment.

sentences.zh: 光弼命荔非元禮出勁卒於羊馬城以拒賊。

translations.literal: Guangbi ordered Lifei Yuanli to bring out crack troops at the sheep-and-horse rampart to resist the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi ordered Lifei Yuanli to deploy elite troops on the cavalry rampart to hold the rebels.

sentences.zh: 光弼自於城東北隅建小朱旗以望賊。

translations.literal: Guangbi himself set up a small vermilion flag at the northeast corner of the wall to watch the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi himself raised a small vermilion banner at the northeast corner of the wall to observe the enemy.

sentences.zh: 賊恃其眾，直進逼城，以車載攻具自隨，督眾填塹，三面各八道以過兵，又開柵為門。

translations.literal: The rebels relied on their numbers, marched straight forward and pressed the wall, bringing siege engines on wagons, supervising the host to fill the moat—eight paths on each of three sides for troops to pass—and also opened the palisade as a gate.
translations.idiomatic: Trusting in their numbers, the rebels pressed straight toward the walls with siege engines on wagons, driving their men to fill the moat. On three sides they opened eight lanes each for troops to cross, and they cut gates through the palisades.

sentences.zh: 光弼望賊逼城，使問元禮曰：「中丞視賊填塹開柵過兵，晏然不動，何也？」

translations.literal: Guangbi, seeing the rebels press the wall, sent to ask Yuanli: "The vice censor watches the rebels fill the moat, open the palisade, and pass troops—yet sits utterly unmoved. Why?"
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the enemy close on the walls, Guangbi sent to ask Yuanli, "You watch them fill the moat, break through the palisades, and march troops across, yet you sit perfectly still. Why?

sentences.zh: 元禮曰：「司空欲守乎，戰乎？」

translations.literal: Yuanli said: "Does the Minister of Works wish to hold or to fight?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuanli replied, "Do you mean to hold the city, or to fight?

sentences.zh: 光弼曰：「欲戰。」

translations.literal: Guangbi said: "I wish to fight."
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi said, "To fight.

sentences.zh: 元禮曰：「欲戰，則賊為吾填塹，何為禁之？」

translations.literal: Yuanli said: "If you wish to fight, then let the rebels fill the moat for us—why forbid it?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuanli said, "If you mean to fight, let them fill the moat for us. Why stop them?

sentences.zh: 光弼曰：「善，吾所不及，勉之！」

translations.literal: Guangbi said: "Good—you see what I miss. Press on!"
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi said, "Well said. That is beyond my reach. Press on!

sentences.zh: 元禮俟柵開，帥敢死士突出擊賊，卻走數百步。

translations.literal: Yuanli waited until the palisade opened, then led dare-to-die warriors in a sudden sally against the rebels and drove them back several hundred paces.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanli waited until the palisade gate was opened, then led his death-defying troops in a sudden charge and drove the enemy back several hundred paces.

sentences.zh: 元禮度賊陣堅，未易摧陷，乃復引退，須其怠而擊之。

translations.literal: Yuanli judged the rebel formation solid and not easy to break; he therefore drew back again to wait until they slackened, then strike.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanli judged the enemy line too firm to break at once, so he withdrew again to wait until they slackened before striking.

sentences.zh: 光弼望見元禮退，怒，遣左右召，欲斬之。

translations.literal: Guangbi, seeing Yuanli withdraw, was angry and sent attendants to summon him, intending to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangbi saw Yuanli fall back, he flew into a rage, sent attendants to summon him, and meant to behead him.

sentences.zh: 元禮曰：「戰正急，召何為？」

translations.literal: Yuanli said: "The battle is at its hottest—why summon me?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuanli said, "The fighting is at its height. Why summon me now?

sentences.zh: 乃退入柵中。

translations.literal: He then withdrew into the palisade.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew back into the palisade.

sentences.zh: 賊亦不敢逼。

translations.literal: The rebels also did not dare press close.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels did not dare press him further.

sentences.zh: 良久，鼓噪出柵門，奮擊，破之。

translations.literal: After a long while he raised a clamor and sallied from the palisade gate, struck fiercely, and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he raised a battle cry, burst from the palisade gate, struck hard, and broke the enemy.

sentences.zh: 周摯復收兵趣北城。

translations.literal: Zhou Zhi gathered his troops again and hastened to the north city.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zhi regrouped and hurried toward the north city.

sentences.zh: 光弼遽帥眾入北城，登城望賊曰：「賊兵雖多，囂而不整，不足畏也。

translations.literal: Guangbi hastily led his host into the north city, mounted the wall, looked at the rebels and said: "Rebel troops are many, but they are noisy and not in order—not worth fearing.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi hurried his troops into the north city, mounted the wall, looked out at the enemy, and said, "Their numbers are great, but they are noisy and disordered. There is nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 不過日中，保為諸君破之。」

translations.literal: Before noon passes, I guarantee I will break them for you all."
translations.idiomatic: Before noon I pledge to break them for you.

sentences.zh: 乃命諸將出戰。

translations.literal: He then ordered the generals out to battle.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered his generals into battle.

sentences.zh: 及期，不決，召諸將問曰：「向來賊陣，何方最堅？」

translations.literal: When the time came, he did not commit; he summoned the generals and asked: "In the rebel formation just now, which quarter was stoutest?"
translations.idiomatic: When the hour came he held back. He summoned his generals and asked, "In the enemy line just now, which sector was strongest?

sentences.zh: 曰：「西北隅。」

translations.literal: They said: "The northwest corner."
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "The northwest corner.

sentences.zh: 光弼命其將郝廷玉當之。

translations.literal: Guangbi ordered his general Hao Tingyu to take it on.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi ordered his general Hao Tingyu to face it.

sentences.zh: 廷玉請騎兵五百，與之三百。

translations.literal: Tingyu requested five hundred cavalry; he was given three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Tingyu asked for five hundred horsemen and was given three hundred.

sentences.zh: 又問其次堅者。

translations.literal: He again asked which was next stoutest.
translations.idiomatic: He asked next which sector was second strongest.

sentences.zh: 曰：「東南隅。

translations.literal: They said: "The southeast corner.
translations.idiomatic: They said, "The southeast corner.

sentences.zh: 光弼命其將論惟貞當之。

translations.literal: Guangbi ordered his general Lun Weizhen to take it on.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi ordered his general Lun Weizhen to face it.

sentences.zh: 惟貞請鐵騎三百，與之二百。

translations.literal: Weizhen requested three hundred iron cavalry; he was given two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhen asked for three hundred armored horsemen and was given two hundred.

sentences.zh: 光弼令諸將曰：「爾輩望吾旗而戰，吾颭旗緩，任爾擇利而戰；

translations.literal: Guangbi instructed the generals: "You all fight by watching my flag. When I wave the flag slowly, you may choose your own advantage in fighting;
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi told his generals, "Fight by my banner. When I wave it slowly, choose your own moment and ground;

sentences.zh: 吾急颭旗三至地，則萬眾齊入，死生以之，少退者斬！」

translations.literal: when I urgently wave the flag thrice to the ground, then the whole host charges together—life or death on it; whoever retreats even slightly is beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: when I whip the banner three times to the ground, the whole army charges as one. Life or death on that stroke. Anyone who falls back even a step will be beheaded!

sentences.zh: 又以短刀置靴中，曰：「戰，危事。

translations.literal: He also placed a short knife in his boot and said: "Battle is a perilous affair.
translations.idiomatic: He also tucked a short knife into his boot and said, "War is perilous.

sentences.zh: 吾國之三公，不可死賊手。

translations.literal: Our state's three dukes must not die by rebel hands.
translations.idiomatic: A grand minister of our state must not die at rebel hands.

sentences.zh: 萬一戰不利，諸君前死於敵，我自剄於此，不令諸君獨死也。」

translations.literal: If by any chance the battle goes ill, you gentlemen go die upon the enemy first; I will cut my own throat here—I will not let you gentlemen die alone."
translations.idiomatic: If the battle goes badly, you go die on the enemy first. I will cut my own throat here. I will not let you die alone.

sentences.zh: 諸將出戰，頃之，廷玉奔還。

translations.literal: The generals went out to battle; before long Tingyu came galloping back.
translations.idiomatic: The generals went out to fight. Before long Tingyu came galloping back.

sentences.zh: 光弼望之，驚曰：「廷玉退，吾事危矣！」

translations.literal: Guangbi saw him and exclaimed in alarm: "Tingyu has retreated—my cause is in peril!"
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi saw him and cried in alarm, "Tingyu has fallen back. All is lost!

sentences.zh: 命左右取廷玉首，廷玉曰：「馬中箭，非敢退也。」

translations.literal: He ordered his attendants to take Tingyu's head; Tingyu said: "My horse was struck by an arrow—I did not dare retreat."
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his attendants to take Tingyu's head. Tingyu said, "My horse was hit. I did not mean to retreat.

sentences.zh: 使者馳報。

translations.literal: The messenger galloped back to report.
translations.idiomatic: The messenger galloped back with the report.

sentences.zh: 光弼令易馬，遣之。

translations.literal: Guangbi ordered a horse change and sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi had his horse changed and sent him back into the fight.

sentences.zh: 僕固懷恩及其子開府儀同三司瑒戰小卻，光弼又命取其首。

translations.literal: Pugu Huai'en and his son Kaifu yitong sansi Yang fought with a slight setback; Guangbi again ordered their heads taken.
translations.idiomatic: Pugu Huai'en and his son Yang, a Kaifu yitong sansi, gave ground slightly in the fighting, and Guangbi again ordered their heads taken.

sentences.zh: 懷恩父子顧見使者提刀馳來，更前決戰。

translations.literal: Father and son Huai'en looked back, saw the messenger galloping up with drawn blade, and pressed forward again to decide the battle.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son Huai'en looked back, saw the messenger galloping toward them with blade drawn, and pressed forward again to fight to the finish.

sentences.zh: 光弼連颭其旗，諸將齊進致死，呼聲動天地，賊眾大潰，斬首千餘級，捕虜五百人，溺死者千餘人。

translations.literal: Guangbi waved his flag repeatedly; the generals advanced together unto death; their shouts shook heaven and earth; the rebel host broke utterly—heads cut over a thousand, captives five hundred, drowned over a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi whipped his banner again and again. The generals charged together as if unto death. Their battle cries shook heaven and earth. The rebel army collapsed completely. More than a thousand heads were taken, five hundred captives seized, and more than a thousand drowned.

sentences.zh: 周摯以數騎遁去，擒其大將徐璜玉、李秦授，其河南節度使安太清走保懷州。

translations.literal: Zhou Zhi escaped with a few horsemen; their great generals Xu Huangyu and Li Qinshou were captured; their Henan military governor An Taiqing fled to hold Huai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zhi escaped with a few horsemen. The rebel generals Xu Huangyu and Li Qinshou were captured. An Taiqing, their Henan military governor, fled to hold Huai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 思明不知摯敗，尚攻南城，光弼驅俘囚臨河示之，乃遁。

translations.literal: Siming did not know Zhi had been defeated and was still attacking the south city; Guangbi drove captives to the riverbank to show them, and then they fled."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Siming did not know Zhou Zhi had been beaten and was still attacking the south city. Guangbi paraded captives along the river to show them, and then the rebels withdrew."

sentences.zh: 丁巳，以李日越為右金吾大將軍。

translations.literal: On dingsi, Li Riyue was made Grand General of the Right Golden Guard.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, Li Riyue was appointed Grand General of the Right Golden Guard.

sentences.zh: 邛、簡、嘉、眉、瀘、戎等州蠻反。

translations.literal: The barbarians of Qiong, Jian, Jia, Mei, Lu, Rong and other prefectures rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The tribal peoples of Qiong, Jian, Jia, Mei, Lu, Rong, and other prefectures rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 十一月，甲子，以殿中監董秦為陝西、神策兩軍兵馬使，賜姓李，名忠臣。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on jiazi, Palace Supervisor Dong Qin was made military commissioner of the two armies of Shaanxi and Shence; he was granted the surname Li and the name Zhongchen.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on jiazi, Palace Supervisor Dong Qin was made military commissioner of the Shaanxi and Shence armies. He was granted the surname Li and given the name Zhongchen.

sentences.zh: 康楚元等眾至萬餘人，商州刺史、充荊襄等道租庸使韋倫發兵討之，駐於鄧之境，招諭降者，厚撫之；

translations.literal: Kang Chuyuan and others, their host exceeding ten thousand, were attacked by Shang Prefecture governor and commissioner for Jing-Xiang circuit grain tax Wei Lun, who encamped on the border of Deng, summoned and instructed those who would surrender, and treated them generously;
translations.idiomatic: Kang Chuyuan and his followers numbered more than ten thousand. Wei Lun, governor of Shang Prefecture and grain-tax commissioner for the Jing and Xiang circuits, raised troops against them, encamped on the border of Deng, summoned those willing to surrender, and treated them generously;

sentences.zh: 伺其稍怠，進軍擊之，生擒楚元，其眾遂潰；

translations.literal: watching for when they slackened slightly, he advanced and struck, captured Chuyuan alive, and their host then broke;
translations.idiomatic: when he saw them slacken, he advanced and attacked, captured Chuyuan alive, and their force broke apart;

sentences.zh: 得其所掠租庸二百萬緡，荊、襄皆平。

translations.literal: recovering two million strings of grain tax they had plundered; Jing and Xiang were both pacified.
translations.idiomatic: recovered two million strings of plundered grain tax, and Jing and Xiang were both pacified.

sentences.zh: 倫，見素之從祖弟也。

translations.literal: Lun was a younger cousin of Jian Su on the paternal side.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Lun was a younger cousin of Pei Jian Su on his father's side.

sentences.zh: 發安西、北庭兵屯陝，以備史思明。

translations.literal: Anxi and Beiting troops were dispatched to encamp at Shan as a precaution against Shi Siming.
translations.idiomatic: Troops from Anxi and Beiting were sent to encamp at Shan as a precaution against Shi Siming.

sentences.zh: 第五琦作乾元錢、重輪錢，與開元錢三品並行，民爭盜鑄，貨輕物重，谷價騰踴，餓殍相望。

translations.literal: Diwu Qi made Qianyuan coins and double-rim coins, which circulated alongside Kaiyuan coins in three denominations; the people vied to illicitly cast them; money grew light and goods heavy; grain prices soared; the starving lay in sight of one another.
translations.idiomatic: Diwu Qi introduced Qianyuan coins and double-rim coins to circulate alongside Kaiyuan coins in three denominations. The people rushed to illicit casting. Money grew light and goods heavy; grain prices soared, and the starving lay everywhere in sight of one another.

sentences.zh: 上言者皆歸咎於琦，庚午，貶琦忠州長史。

translations.literal: Memorialists all blamed Qi; on gengwu Qi was demoted to prefectural administrator of Zhong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Memorialists all blamed Diwu Qi. On gengwu he was demoted to prefectural administrator of Zhong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫賀蘭進明貶溱州員外司馬，坐琦黨也。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Helan Jinming was demoted to supernumerary adjutant of Qin Prefecture, implicated as Qi's partisan.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Helan Jinming was demoted to supernumerary adjutant of Qin Prefecture for association with Qi's faction.

sentences.zh: 十二月，甲午，呂諲領度支使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on jiawu, Lü Yin took charge as commissioner of the census.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on jiawu, Lü Yin took charge as commissioner of the census.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，韋倫送康楚元詣闕，斬之。

translations.literal: On yisi, Wei Lun sent Kang Chuyuan to the capital; he was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, Wei Lun sent Kang Chuyuan to the capital, where he was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 史思明遣其將李歸仁將鐵騎五千寇陝州，神策兵馬使衛伯玉以數百騎擊破之於礓子阪，得馬六百匹，歸仁走。

translations.literal: Shi Siming sent his general Li Guiren with five thousand iron cavalry to raid Shan Prefecture; Shence military commissioner Wei Boyu with several hundred horsemen defeated them at Jiangzi Slope, took six hundred horses, and Guiren fled.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Siming sent his general Li Guiren with five thousand armored horsemen to raid Shan Prefecture. Wei Boyu, military commissioner of the Shence army, defeated them at Jiangzi Slope with several hundred horsemen, seized six hundred horses, and Guiren fled.

sentences.zh: 以伯玉為鎮西四鎮行營節度使。

translations.literal: Boyu was made military commissioner of the expeditionary headquarters of the Four Garrisons west of the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Boyu was appointed military commissioner of the expeditionary headquarters of the Four Garrisons west of the pass.

sentences.zh: 李忠臣與歸仁等戰於永寧、莎柵之間，屢破之。

translations.literal: Li Zhongchen fought Guiren and others between Yongning and Sha Palisade and repeatedly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhongchen fought Guiren and his men between Yongning and Sha Palisade and repeatedly defeated them.

sentences.zh: 肅宗文明武德大聖大宣孝皇帝下之上上元元年（

translations.literal: The latter part of the reign of Emperor Suzong, Cultured and Martial, Greatly Sagely and Greatly Promulgating, Filially Pious—above, Shangyuan year 1 (
translations.idiomatic: The latter part of the reign of Emperor Suzong of Tang—Shangyuan year 1 (

sentences.zh: 庚子，公元七六零年）

translations.literal: gengzi, AD 760)
translations.idiomatic: gengzi, AD 760)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛巳，以李光弼為太尉兼中書令，餘如故。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on xinsi, Li Guangbi was made Grand Marshal and concurrently Director of the Secretariat; the rest unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on xinsi of the first month, Li Guangbi was appointed Grand Marshal and concurrently Director of the Secretariat; his other offices remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，以于闐王勝之弟曜同四鎮節度副使，權知本國事。

translations.literal: On bingxu, Yao, younger brother of Khotan king Sheng, was made deputy military commissioner of the Four Garrisons, with provisional charge of his state's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, Yao, younger brother of the king of Khotan, Sheng, was made deputy military commissioner of the Four Garrisons with provisional charge of the affairs of his kingdom.

sentences.zh: 党項等羌吞噬邊鄙，將逼京畿，乃分邠寧等州節度為鄜坊丹延節度，亦謂之渭北節度。

translations.literal: Tangut and other Qiang peoples devoured the border marches and were about to press the capital region; the Binning circuit and other prefecture garrisons were therefore divided into the Yao-Fang-Dan-Yan circuit, also called the North-of-Wei circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangut and other Qiang peoples were swallowing the frontier and threatening the capital region. The Binning circuit was therefore split off into the Yao-Fang-Dan-Yan circuit, also called the North-of-Wei circuit.

sentences.zh: 以邠州刺史桑如珪領邠寧，鄜州刺史杜冕領鄜坊節度副使，分道招討。

translations.literal: Bin Prefecture governor Sang Rugui took Binning; Yao Prefecture governor Du Mian took deputy military commissioner of Yao-Fang, each proceeding by separate routes to summon and suppress.
translations.idiomatic: Sang Rugui, governor of Bin Prefecture, took command of Binning, and Du Mian, governor of Yao Prefecture, became deputy military commissioner of Yao-Fang. They set out by separate routes to summon rebels and suppress them.

sentences.zh: 戊子，以郭子儀領兩道節度使，留京師，假其威名以鎮之。

translations.literal: On wuzi, Guo Ziyi was made military commissioner of both circuits, remaining in the capital—his prestige borrowed to quiet the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, Guo Ziyi was made military commissioner of both circuits and remained in the capital, his prestige alone relied upon to keep the frontier calm.

sentences.zh: 上祀九宮貴神。

translations.literal: The emperor sacrificed to the noble spirits of the Nine Palaces.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sacrificed to the spirits of the Nine Palaces.

sentences.zh: 二月，李光弼攻懷州，史思明救之。

translations.literal: In the second month, Li Guangbi attacked Huai Prefecture; Shi Siming went to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Li Guangbi attacked Huai Prefecture, and Shi Siming marched to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，光弼逆戰於沁水之上，破之，斬首三千餘級。

translations.literal: On guimao, Guangbi met them in battle on the Qin River and defeated them, cutting heads exceeding three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, Guangbi met the enemy on the Qin River, defeated them, and took more than three thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 忠州長史第五琦既行，或告琦受人金二百兩，遣御史劉期光追按之。

translations.literal: After Prefectural Administrator of Zhong Diwu Qi had set out, someone reported that Qi had received two hundred liang of gold from a person; the censor Liu Qiguang was sent to pursue and investigate.
translations.idiomatic: After Diwu Qi had set out on his way to Zhong Prefecture as prefectural administrator, someone reported that he had accepted two hundred liang of gold. The censor Liu Qiguang was sent to pursue and investigate.

sentences.zh: 琦曰：「琦備位宰相，二百兩金不可手挈；

translations.literal: Qi said: "Qi holds a place among Grand Chancellors—two hundred liang of gold cannot be carried in hand;
translations.idiomatic: Qi said, "I held a place among grand chancellors. Two hundred liang of gold cannot be carried in one's hand;

sentences.zh: 若付受有憑，請准律科罪。」

translations.literal: if there is proof of receipt and payment, I ask that the law be applied and punishment assigned."
translations.idiomatic: if there is proof of receipt, I ask that the law be applied and punishment assigned accordingly.

sentences.zh: 期光即奏琦已服罪。

translations.literal: Qiguang at once memorialized that Qi had already confessed guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Qiguang at once memorialized that Qi had already confessed guilt.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，琦坐除名，長流夷州。

translations.literal: On gengxu, Qi was stripped of his name and exiled far to Yi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, Qi was stripped of rank and exiled far to Yi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 三月，甲申，改蒲州為河中府。

translations.literal: In the third month, on jiashen, Pu Prefecture was changed to Hezhong Prefecture-fu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jiashen, Pu Prefecture was redesignated Hezhong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，李光弼破安太清於懷州城下，夏，四月，壬辰，破史思明於河陽西渚，斬首千五百餘級。

translations.literal: On gengyin, Li Guangbi defeated An Taiqing below Huai Prefecture city; summer, fourth month, on renchen, he defeated Shi Siming at the west shoal of Heyang, cutting heads exceeding fifteen hundred.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, Li Guangbi defeated An Taiqing below the walls of Huai Prefecture. In summer, on renchen of the fourth month, he defeated Shi Siming at the west shoal of Heyang and took more than fifteen hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 襄州將張維瑾、曹玠殺節度使史翽，據州反。

translations.literal: Xiang Prefecture generals Zhang Weijin and Cao Jie killed military governor Shi Chi and seized the prefecture in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiang Prefecture generals Zhang Weijin and Cao Jie killed military governor Shi Chi, seized the prefecture, and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 制以隴州刺史韋倫為山南東道節度使。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Long Prefecture governor Wei Lun as military governor of Shannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Wei Lun, governor of Long Prefecture, military governor of Shannan East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 時李輔國用事，節度使皆出其門。

translations.literal: At the time Li Fuguo held power; military governors all came from his faction.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Li Fuguo held power, and military governors were all drawn from his faction.

sentences.zh: 倫既朝廷所除，又不謁輔國，尋改秦州防禦使。

translations.literal: Lun had been appointed by the court yet did not pay court to Fuguo; soon he was changed to defensive commissioner of Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Lun had been appointed by the court yet did not call on Li Fuguo. Soon he was reassigned as defensive commissioner of Qin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 己未，以陝西節度使來瑱為山南東道節度使。

translations.literal: On jiwei, Shaanxi military governor Lai Tian was made military governor of Shannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, Lai Tian, military governor of Shaanxi, was appointed military governor of Shannan East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 瑱至襄州，張維瑾等皆降。

translations.literal: When Tian reached Xiang Prefecture, Zhang Weijin and the others all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When Lai Tian reached Xiang Prefecture, Zhang Weijin and the others all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 閏月，丁卯，加河東節度使王思禮為司空。

translations.literal: Intercalary month, day dingmao, Wang Silun, military commissioner of Hedong, was additionally appointed Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on dingmao, Wang Silun, military commissioner of Hedong, was additionally appointed Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 自武德以來，思禮始不為宰相而拜三公。

translations.literal: Since Wude, Silun was the first not to be chancellor yet to be appointed to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Wude era, Silun was the first man appointed to one of the Three Dukes without having served as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，徙趙王系為越王。

translations.literal: On day jiaxu, Prince of Zhao Xi was transferred to Prince of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, Prince of Zhao Xi was reassigned as Prince of Yue.

sentences.zh: 己卯，赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: On day jimao, a general amnesty was proclaimed and the reign title was changed.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao, the emperor proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the reign title.

sentences.zh: 追謚太公望為武成王，選歷代名將為亞聖、十哲。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed Taigong Wang as King Wu Cheng; selected famous generals through the ages as Sub-Sage and Ten Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Taigong Wang was posthumously ennobled as King Wu Cheng, and celebrated generals from history were chosen as Sub-Sage and Ten Worthies.

sentences.zh: 其中祀、下祀並雜祀一切並停。

translations.literal: Among these, mid-level sacrifices, lower sacrifices, and all miscellaneous sacrifices were entirely suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-tier, lower-tier, and all miscellaneous rites among them were suspended entirely.

sentences.zh: 是日，史思明入東京。

translations.literal: That day, Shi Siming entered the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Shi Siming entered the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 五月，丙午，以太子太傅苗晉卿行侍中。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day bingwu, Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent Miao Jinqing was appointed acting chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on bingwu, Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent Miao Jinqing was appointed acting chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 晉卿練達吏事，而謹身固位，時人比之胡廣。

translations.literal: Jinqing was practiced in official affairs, yet guarded his person and held his position; men of the time compared him to Hu Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Jinqing was skilled in administrative matters, but he guarded his own person and clung to his post; contemporaries compared him to Hu Guang.

sentences.zh: 宦者馬上言受賂，為人求官於兵部侍郎、同中書門下三品呂諲，諲為之補官。

translations.literal: Eunuch Ma Shangyan took bribes and sought office for someone from Vice Minister of War and Associate Grand Councillor Lü Yin; Yin filled the appointment for him.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Ma Shangyan took bribes and asked Vice Minister of War and Associate Grand Councillor Lü Yin to secure an office for someone; Yin granted it.

sentences.zh: 事覺，上言杖死。

translations.literal: When the matter came to light, Shangyan was beaten to death by imperial order.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair came to light, Shangyan was ordered flogged to death.

sentences.zh: 壬子，諲罷為太子賓客。

translations.literal: On day renzi, Yin was dismissed and made guest of the heir.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, Yin was dismissed and appointed guest of the heir.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，以京兆尹南華劉晏為戶部侍郎，充度支、鑄錢、鹽鐵等使。

translations.literal: On day guichou, Liu Yan of Nanhua, intendant of the capital district, was appointed vice minister of revenue and made commissioner of fiscal affairs, coin minting, salt and iron, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, Liu Yan of Nanhua, intendant of the capital district, was made vice minister of revenue and appointed commissioner of fiscal affairs, coin minting, salt and iron, and related offices.

sentences.zh: 晏善治財利，故用之。

translations.literal: Yan was skilled at managing wealth and profit; therefore he was employed.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was skilled at managing finances, and so he was put in charge.

sentences.zh: 六月，甲子，桂州經略使邢濟奏：破西原蠻二十萬眾，斬其帥黃乾曜等。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day jiazi, regional inspector of Guizhou Xing Ji memorialized: he broke two hundred thousand of the Xiyuan barbarians and beheaded their chieftain Huang Qianyao and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jiazi, Guizhou regional inspector Xing Ji reported that he had broken two hundred thousand Xiyuan tribesmen and beheaded their leader Huang Qianyao and others.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，鳳翔節度使崔光遠奏破涇、隴羌、渾十餘萬眾。

translations.literal: On day yichou, Fengxiang military commissioner Cui Guangyuan memorialized that he had broken more than one hundred thousand Qiang and Hun of Jing and Long.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, Fengxiang military commissioner Cui Guangyuan reported breaking more than one hundred thousand Qiang and Hun tribesmen in Jing and Long.

sentences.zh: 三品錢行浸久，屬歲荒，米斗至七千錢，人相食。

translations.literal: Third-rank coin had circulated increasingly long; coinciding with a year of famine, a dou of rice reached seven thousand cash; people ate one another.
translations.idiomatic: The devalued third-rank coinage had been in circulation for some time; famine followed, and a peck of rice fetched seven thousand cash until people turned to cannibalism.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹鄭叔清捕私鑄錢者，數月間，榜死者八百餘人，不能禁。

translations.literal: Capital intendant Zheng Shuqing arrested private coiners; within a few months over eight hundred died on the whipping post, yet it could not be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Capital intendant Zheng Shuqing cracked down on illegal minting; within months more than eight hundred died under the lash, yet the practice could not be stopped.

sentences.zh: 乃敕京畿，開元錢與乾元小錢皆當十，其重輪錢當三十，諸州更俟進止。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict was issued for the capital region: Kaiyuan coins and Qianyuan small coins were both valued at ten; heavy-rim coins at thirty; other prefectures were to await further orders.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then fixed valuations in the capital region: Kaiyuan and Qianyuan small coins at ten each, heavy-rim coins at thirty; other prefectures were told to await further instruction.

sentences.zh: 是時史思明亦鑄順天、得一錢，一當開元錢百。

translations.literal: At this time Shi Siming also minted Shuntian and Deyi coins, each worth one hundred Kaiyuan coins.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Siming was minting Shuntian and Deyi coins at the same time, each reckoned at one hundred Kaiyuan coins.

sentences.zh: 賊中物價尤貴。

translations.literal: Prices within the rebel territory were especially high.
translations.idiomatic: Prices in rebel-held territory were even higher.

sentences.zh: 甲申，興王佋薨。

translations.literal: On day jiashen, Prince of Xing You died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, Prince of Xing You died.

sentences.zh: 佋，張后長子也，幼曰定王侗。

translations.literal: You was the eldest son of Empress Zhang; in youth he was called Prince of Ding Tong.
translations.idiomatic: You was Empress Zhang's eldest son; in his youth he had been Prince of Ding, named Tong.

sentences.zh: 張后以故數欲危太子，太子常以恭遜取容。

translations.literal: Empress Zhang for this reason repeatedly wished to endanger the heir; the heir often used deference to win favor.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason Empress Zhang repeatedly tried to undermine the heir, who in turn often sought safety through humble deference.

sentences.zh: 會佋薨，侗尚幼，太子位遂定。

translations.literal: When You died, Tong was still young, and the heir's position was thus settled.
translations.idiomatic: You's death came while Tong was still young, and the heir's position was at last secured.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，鳳翔節度使崔光遠破党項於普潤。

translations.literal: On day yiyou, Fengxiang military commissioner Cui Guangyuan broke the Tangut at Purun.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, Fengxiang military commissioner Cui Guangyuan defeated the Tangut at Purun.

sentences.zh: 平盧兵馬使田神功奏破史思明之兵於鄭州。

translations.literal: Pinglu army-and-horse commissioner Tian Shengong memorialized that he had broken Shi Siming's army at Zheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Pinglu army-and-horse commissioner Tian Shengong reported defeating Shi Siming's forces at Zheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 上皇愛興慶宮，自蜀歸，即居之。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor loved Xingqing Palace; returning from Shu, he took up residence there at once.
translations.idiomatic: The Retired Emperor loved Xingqing Palace and moved in there as soon as he returned from Shu.

sentences.zh: 上時自夾城往起居，上皇亦間至大明宮。

translations.literal: The emperor often went via the walled passage to inquire after his health; the Retired Emperor also occasionally went to Daming Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor visited him regularly through the walled passage, and the Retired Emperor also occasionally came to Daming Palace.

sentences.zh: 左龍武大將軍陳玄禮、內侍監高力士久侍衛上皇；

translations.literal: Left Longwu Grand General Chen Xuanli and palace internuncio Gao Lishi had long attended and guarded the Retired Emperor;
translations.idiomatic: Left Longwu Grand General Chen Xuanli and chief eunuch Gao Lishi had long attended the Retired Emperor;

sentences.zh: 上又命玉真公主、如仙媛、內侍王承恩、魏悅及梨園弟子常娛侍左右。

translations.literal: the emperor also ordered Princess Yuzhen, Ru Xianyuan, eunuchs Wang Chengen and Wei Yue, and Pear Garden performers to attend constantly on his left and right for amusement.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor also assigned Princess Yuzhen, Lady Ru Xianyuan, eunuchs Wang Chengen and Wei Yue, and Pear Garden performers to amuse him constantly.

sentences.zh: 上皇多御長慶樓，父老過者往往瞻拜，呼萬歲，上皇常於樓下置酒食賜之；

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor often took the Changqing Tower; when elders passed by they often looked up in homage and cried "Ten thousand years"; the Retired Emperor often set out food and drink below the tower to bestow upon them;
translations.idiomatic: The Retired Emperor often sat on the Changqing Tower; common folk who passed below would look up in homage and shout "Long live the Emperor!" and he often had food and drink set out below for them;

sentences.zh: 又嘗召將軍郭英乂等上樓賜宴。

translations.literal: He also once summoned Generals Guo Yingyi and others up the tower for a banquet.
translations.idiomatic: He also once summoned Generals Guo Yingyi and others to the tower for a feast.

sentences.zh: 有劍南奏事官過樓下拜舞，上皇命玉真公主、如仙媛為之作主人。

translations.literal: A Jiannan memorial officer passed below the tower and performed the bow-and-dance; the Retired Emperor ordered Princess Yuzhen and Ru Xianyuan to act as hostesses for him.
translations.idiomatic: When a Jiannan memorial officer passed below and performed the court bow, the Retired Emperor had Princess Yuzhen and Lady Ru Xianyuan receive him as hostesses.

sentences.zh: 李輔國素微賤，雖暴貴用事，上皇左右皆輕之。

translations.literal: Li Fuguo had always been of base origin; though he rose suddenly to power, those around the Retired Emperor all looked down on him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fuguo came from humble origins; though he had risen abruptly to power, the Retired Emperor's attendants all looked down on him.

sentences.zh: 輔國意恨，且欲立奇功以固其寵，乃言於上曰：「上皇居興慶宮，日與外人交通，陳玄禮、高力士謀不利於陛下。

translations.literal: Fuguo nursed resentment and also wished to establish extraordinary merit to secure his favor; he therefore said to the emperor: "The Retired Emperor dwells at Xingqing Palace, daily consorting with outsiders; Chen Xuanli and Gao Lishi plot harm to Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo nursed a grievance and sought a bold stroke to cement his favor. He told the emperor, "The Retired Emperor lives at Xingqing Palace and meets outsiders every day. Chen Xuanli and Gao Lishi are plotting against Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 今六軍將士盡靈武勳臣，皆反仄不安，臣曉諭不能解，不敢不以聞。」

translations.literal: Now the six-army officers and soldiers are all meritorious men of Lingwu; all are uneasy and restive; though I have exhorted them I cannot relieve their anxiety—I dare not fail to report this."
translations.idiomatic: The six armies are filled with the men who earned their merit at Lingwu, and they are all uneasy. I have tried to reason with them but cannot calm them. I dare not keep this from you."

sentences.zh: 上泣曰：「聖皇慈仁，豈容有此！」

translations.literal: The emperor wept and said: "The Holy Emperor is benevolent—how could he allow such a thing!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept and said, "The Holy Emperor is benevolent—how could such a thing be possible!"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「上皇固無此意，其如群小何！

translations.literal: He replied: "The Retired Emperor surely has no such intent—but what of the petty men around him!
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo replied, "The Retired Emperor surely has no such intent—but what of the petty men at his side!

sentences.zh: 陛下為天下主，當為社稷大計，消亂於未萌，豈得徇匹夫之孝！

translations.literal: Your Majesty is lord of all under Heaven; you should plan for the altars of state, quell disorder before it sprouts—how can you indulge private filial feeling!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is sovereign of the realm. You must think of the altars of state and stamp out trouble before it takes root. How can you indulge private filial feeling!

sentences.zh: 且興慶宮與閭閻相參，垣墉淺露，非至尊所宜居。

translations.literal: Moreover Xingqing Palace adjoins common lanes; its walls are shallow and exposed—not a place fit for the utmost honored one to dwell.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Xingqing Palace stands amid ordinary streets, its walls low and exposed—not a fit dwelling for the utmost honored one.

sentences.zh: 大內深嚴，奉迎居之，與彼何殊，又得杜絕小人熒惑聖聽。

translations.literal: The Inner Palace is deep and stern; receive him to dwell there—how is that different from the other?—and moreover you can cut off petty men's sway over the holy ear.
translations.idiomatic: The Inner Palace is deep and secure. If he is received there, what difference is there for him? And petty men could no longer sway his judgment.

sentences.zh: 如此，上皇享萬歲之安，陛下有三朝之樂，庸何傷乎！」

translations.literal: Thus the Retired Emperor would enjoy the safety of ten thousand years, Your Majesty would have the joy of the three audiences—where is the harm!"
translations.idiomatic: In that way the Retired Emperor would enjoy lasting safety, and Your Majesty the pleasure of daily audiences. What would be lost!"

sentences.zh: 上不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 興慶宮先有馬三百匹，輔國矯敕取之，才留十匹。

translations.literal: Xingqing Palace first had three hundred horses; Fuguo forged an edict and took them, leaving only ten.
translations.idiomatic: Xingqing Palace had three hundred horses; Fuguo forged an edict and seized them, leaving only ten.

sentences.zh: 上皇謂高力士曰：「吾兒為輔國所惑，不得終孝矣。」

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor said to Gao Lishi: "My son is deluded by Fuguo—I can no longer fulfill filial piety to the end."
translations.idiomatic: The Retired Emperor told Gao Lishi, "My son has been led astray by Fuguo. I shall not be able to keep my filial duty to the end."

sentences.zh: 輔國又令六軍將士，號哭叩頭，請迎上皇居西內。

translations.literal: Fuguo also ordered the six-army officers and soldiers to wail and knock their heads, requesting that the Retired Emperor be received to dwell in the Western Inner Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo then had officers and soldiers of the six armies wail and prostrate themselves, begging that the Retired Emperor be moved to the Western Inner Palace.

sentences.zh: 上泣不應。

translations.literal: The emperor wept and did not assent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept and gave no answer.

sentences.zh: 輔國懼。

translations.literal: Fuguo was afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo grew afraid.

sentences.zh: 會上不豫，秋，七月，丁未，輔國矯稱上語，迎上皇游西內，至睿武門，輔國將射生五百騎，露刃遮道奏曰：「皇帝以興慶宮湫隘，迎上皇遷居大內。」

translations.literal: When the emperor was unwell, autumn, seventh month, day dingwei, Fuguo falsely claimed the emperor's words and received the Retired Emperor to tour the Western Inner Palace; reaching Ruiwu Gate, Fuguo led five hundred mounted archers, bared blades blocking the road, and reported: "The emperor, because Xingqing Palace is cramped and damp, receives the Retired Emperor to move and dwell in the Great Inner Palace."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell ill, in the seventh month of autumn, on dingwei, Fuguo forged the emperor's orders and escorted the Retired Emperor toward the Western Inner Palace. At Ruiwu Gate Fuguo led five hundred mounted archers with bared blades blocking the way and announced, "The emperor finds Xingqing Palace cramped and damp and has sent us to receive the Retired Emperor to the Great Inner Palace."

sentences.zh: 上皇驚，幾墜。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor was alarmed and nearly fell.
translations.idiomatic: The Retired Emperor started in alarm and nearly fell from his mount.

sentences.zh: 高力士曰：「李輔國何得無禮！」

translations.literal: Gao Lishi said: "How dare Li Fuguo be so rude!"
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lishi cried, "How dare Li Fuguo show such insolence!

sentences.zh: 叱令下馬。

translations.literal: He shouted, ordering him to dismount.
translations.idiomatic: He shouted and ordered him to dismount.

sentences.zh: 輔國不得已而下。

translations.literal: Fuguo had no choice but to dismount.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo had no choice but to get down.

sentences.zh: 力士因宣上皇誥曰：「諸將士各好在！」

translations.literal: Lishi then proclaimed the Retired Emperor's command: "Officers and soldiers, each take care!"
translations.idiomatic: Lishi then proclaimed on the Retired Emperor's behalf, "Officers and soldiers—all is well!"

sentences.zh: 將士皆納刃，再拜，呼萬歲。

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers all sheathed blades, bowed twice, and cried "Ten thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers sheathed their blades, bowed twice, and shouted "Long live the Emperor!"

sentences.zh: 力士又叱輔國與己共執上皇馬鞚，侍衛如西內，居甘露殿。

translations.literal: Lishi again shouted at Fuguo to grasp the Retired Emperor's horse's bridle together with him, escorting him to the Western Inner Palace, where he dwelt at Ganlu Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Lishi then ordered Fuguo to join him in leading the Retired Emperor's horse into the Western Inner Palace, where he was lodged at Ganlu Hall.

sentences.zh: 輔國帥眾而退。

translations.literal: Fuguo led his host and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo withdrew with his men.

sentences.zh: 所留侍衛兵，才尪老數人。

translations.literal: Of the guard soldiers left behind, there were only a few feeble old men.
translations.idiomatic: Only a handful of feeble old men were left to guard him.

sentences.zh: 陳玄禮、高力士及舊宮人皆不能留左右。

translations.literal: Chen Xuanli, Gao Lishi, and the old palace attendants could none of them remain at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xuanli, Gao Lishi, and the Retired Emperor's longtime attendants were none of them allowed to stay.

sentences.zh: 上皇曰：「興慶宮，吾之王地，吾數以讓皇帝，皇帝不受。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor said: "Xingqing Palace is my princely domain; I have repeatedly offered it to the emperor, but the emperor would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The Retired Emperor said, "Xingqing Palace was my princely estate. I offered it to the emperor again and again, but he would not take it.

sentences.zh: 今日之徙，亦吾志也。」

translations.literal: Today's removal is also my wish."
translations.idiomatic: Today's move is also my wish."

sentences.zh: 是日，輔國與六軍大將素服見上，請罪。

translations.literal: That day, Fuguo and the grand generals of the six armies came in plain dress to see the emperor and asked forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: That day Fuguo and the grand generals of the six armies appeared before the emperor in undyed garments to beg forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 上又迫於諸將，乃勞之曰：「南宮、西內，亦復何殊！

translations.literal: The emperor, pressed again by the generals, then comforted them, saying: "South Palace and Western Inner Palace—what difference is there after all!
translations.idiomatic: Pressed by the generals, the emperor comforted them and said, "South Palace and Western Inner Palace—what difference does it make!

sentences.zh: 卿等恐小人熒惑，防微杜漸，以安社稷，何所懼也！」

translations.literal: You feared petty men misleading him, checked the small to stop the large, to secure the altars of state—what is there to fear!"
translations.idiomatic: You feared petty men might mislead him and took care to check trouble early for the realm's sake. What is there to fear!"

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書顏真卿首帥百寮上表，請問上皇起居。

translations.literal: Minister of Justice Yan Zhenqing led the hundred officials first in submitting a memorial asking after the Retired Emperor's health.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Justice Yan Zhenqing was first among the hundred officials to submit a memorial inquiring after the Retired Emperor's health.

sentences.zh: 輔國惡之，奏貶蓬州長史。

translations.literal: Fuguo hated this and memorialized that he be demoted to chief secretary of Peng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo resented this and had him demoted to chief secretary of Peng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，敕天下重稜錢皆當三十，如畿內。

translations.literal: On day guichou, an edict ordered that throughout the realm heavy-rim coins were all to pass at thirty, as in the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, an edict fixed the valuation of heavy-rim coins empire-wide at thirty, matching the capital region.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，高力士流巫州，王承恩流播州，魏悅流溱州，陳玄禮勒致仕；

translations.literal: On day bingchen, Gao Lishi was banished to Wu Prefecture, Wang Chengen to Bo Prefecture, Wei Yue to Qin Prefecture; Chen Xuanli was compelled to retire;
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Gao Lishi was exiled to Wu, Wang Chengen to Bo, and Wei Yue to Qin; Chen Xuanli was forced to retire;

sentences.zh: 置如仙媛于歸州，玉真公主出居玉真觀。

translations.literal: Ru Xianyuan was placed at Gui Prefecture; Princess Yuzhen went out to dwell at Yuzhen Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ru Xianyuan was sent to Gui Prefecture, and Princess Yuzhen moved out to Yuzhen Abbey.

sentences.zh: 上更選後宮百餘人，置西內，備灑掃。

translations.literal: The emperor further selected more than a hundred from the rear palace, placed them in the Western Inner Palace, and prepared them for sweeping and cleaning.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor chose more than a hundred women from the rear palace and installed them in the Western Inner Palace to attend to housekeeping.

sentences.zh: 令萬安、咸宜二公主視服膳；

translations.literal: He ordered Princesses Wan'an and Xianyi to oversee clothing and food;
translations.idiomatic: He put Princesses Wan'an and Xianyi in charge of his meals and clothing;

sentences.zh: 四方所獻珍異，先薦上皇。

translations.literal: rare and strange tribute from the four directions was first presented to the Retired Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: and rare tribute from the provinces was always presented to the Retired Emperor first.

sentences.zh: 然上皇日以不懌，因不茹葷，辟谷，浸以成疾。

translations.literal: Yet the Retired Emperor grew daily displeased; therefore he ate no meat, abstained from grain, and gradually fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Retired Emperor grew daily more downcast; he gave up meat and grain and slowly sickened.

sentences.zh: 上初猶往問安，既而上亦有疾，但遣人起居。

translations.literal: At first the emperor still went to inquire after his health; afterward the emperor too had illness, and only sent men to ask after his health.
translations.idiomatic: At first the emperor still visited him in person; then he too fell ill and sent messengers only.

sentences.zh: 其後上稍悔寤，惡輔國，欲誅之，畏其握兵，竟猶豫不能決。

translations.literal: Afterward the emperor gradually came to repent and awaken, hated Fuguo, wished to execute him, yet feared his grip on the army and in the end hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor slowly came to his senses, turned against Fuguo, and wanted him dead—but feared his control of the armies and in the end could not bring himself to act.

sentences.zh: 初，哥舒翰破吐蕃於臨洮西關磨環川，於其地置神策軍。

translations.literal: Earlier Geshu Han defeated the Tibetans at Guanmohuan Creek west of Lintao and there established the Shence Army.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Geshu Han defeated the Tibetans at Guanmohuan Creek west of Lintao, he established the Shence Army on that ground.

sentences.zh: 及安祿山反，軍使成如璆遣其將衛伯玉將千人赴難。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, army commissioner Cheng Ruqiu sent his general Wei Boyu to lead a thousand men to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, army commissioner Cheng Ruqiu sent his general Wei Boyu with a thousand men to aid the court.

sentences.zh: 既而軍地淪入吐蕃，伯玉留屯於陝，累官至右羽林大將軍。

translations.literal: Subsequently the army's territory fell into Tibetan hands; Boyu remained garrisoned at Shan and rose through successive posts to Right Pillar-of-State Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: The Shence base later fell to the Tibetans, and Boyu stayed garrisoned at Shan, rising in time to Right Pillar-of-State Grand General.

sentences.zh: 八月，庚午，以伯玉為神策軍節度使。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day gengwu, Boyu was made military commissioner of the Shence Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on gengwu, Boyu was appointed military commissioner of the Shence Army.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，贈謚興王佋曰恭懿太子。

translations.literal: On day dinghai, posthumous title was granted to Prince of Xing You as Reverent and Virtuous Heir.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Prince of Xing You was posthumously ennobled as the Reverent and Virtuous Heir.

sentences.zh: 九月，甲午，置南都於荊州，以荊州為江陵府，仍置永平軍團練兵三千人，以扼吳、蜀之沖，從節度使呂諲之請也。

translations.literal: Ninth month, day jiawu, the Southern Capital was established at Jing Prefecture; Jing Prefecture was made Jiangling Prefecture; three thousand Yongping Army drilled troops were still established to choke the crossroads of Wu and Shu—following the request of military commissioner Lü Yin.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on jiawu, a Southern Capital was established at Jing Prefecture, which was renamed Jiangling Prefecture; three thousand drilled troops of the Yongping Army were stationed there to hold the crossroads between Wu and Shu, at the request of military commissioner Lü Yin.

sentences.zh: 或上言：「天下未平，不宜置郭子儀於散地。」

translations.literal: Someone memorialized the throne: "The realm is not yet pacified—it is not fitting to place Guo Ziyi in an idle post."
translations.idiomatic: Someone memorialized, "The realm is not yet at peace; Guo Ziyi should not be left idle."

sentences.zh: 乙未，命子儀出鎮邠州；

translations.literal: On day yimwei, Ziyi was ordered out to guard Bin Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: On yimwei, Ziyi was ordered to take command at Bin Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 党項遁去。

translations.literal: the Tangut fled away.
translations.idiomatic: and the Tangut withdrew.

sentences.zh: 戊申，制：「子儀統諸道兵自朔方直取范陽，還定河北，發射生英武等禁軍及朔方、鄜坊、邠寧、涇原諸道蕃、漢兵共七萬人，皆受子儀節度。」

translations.literal: On day wushen, an edict: "Ziyi shall command the various circuit armies from Shuofang straight to Fanyang, then return to settle Hebei; dispatch the She Sheng, Yingwu, and other palace armies plus Tangut and Han troops of the Shuofang, Fufang, Binning, and Jingyuan circuits—altogether seventy thousand men—all under Ziyi's command."
translations.idiomatic: On wushen an edict ordered Ziyi to lead allied armies from Shuofang straight against Fanyang, then sweep Hebei; seventy thousand men from the palace guards and the Shuofang, Fufang, Binning, and Jingyuan commands—including both tribal and Han troops—were all placed under his command."

sentences.zh: 制下旬日，復為魚朝恩所沮，事竟不行。

translations.literal: Within ten days of the edict, it was again obstructed by Yu Chao'en, and the matter in the end was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days Yu Chao'en blocked it again, and the plan came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丙子，置青、沂等五州節度使。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day bingzi, military commissioners of five prefectures including Qing and Yi were established.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on bingzi, military commissioners were established for five prefectures including Qing and Yi.

sentences.zh: 十一月，壬辰，涇州破党項。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, day renchen, Jing Prefecture broke the Tangut.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on renchen, Jing Prefecture defeated the Tangut.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞李銑、宋州刺史劉殿皆領淮西節度副使。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Li Xian and Song Prefecture prefect Liu Zhan both held the post of Huai West associate military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Li Xian and Song Prefecture prefect Liu Zhan both served as associate military commissioners of Huai West.

sentences.zh: 銑貪暴不法，展剛強自用，故為其上者多惡之；

translations.literal: Xian was greedy, violent, and lawless; Zhan was stubborn and self-willed—therefore those above them mostly hated them;
translations.idiomatic: Xian was greedy and brutal; Zhan was obstinate and willful. Their superiors mostly despised them both;

sentences.zh: 節度使王仲升先奏銑罪而誅之。

translations.literal: Military commissioner Wang Zhongsheng first memorialized Xian's crimes and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: and military commissioner Wang Zhongsheng memorialized Xian's crimes and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 時有謠言曰：「手執金刀起東方。」

translations.literal: At the time there was a rhyme saying: "Hand grasping golden blade, rising in the east."
translations.idiomatic: A rhyme was going around: "Hand holding the golden blade, rising in the east."

sentences.zh: 仲升使監軍使、內左常侍邢延恩入奏：「展倔強不受命，姓名應謠讖，請除之。」

translations.literal: Zhongsheng sent army overseer and Left Internuncio Xing Yan'en to enter and memorialize: "Zhan is stubborn and will not accept orders; his name responds to the rhyme and omen—I ask that he be removed."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongsheng sent army overseer and Left Internuncio Xing Yan'en to report, "Zhan is defiant and disobedient; his name matches the omen in the rhyme. I ask that he be removed."

sentences.zh: 延恩因說上曰：「展與李銑一體之人，今銑誅，展不自安，苟不去之，恐其為亂。

translations.literal: Yan'en then persuaded the emperor, saying: "Zhan and Li Xian are men of one kind; now that Xian is executed, Zhan is not at ease—if he is not removed, I fear he will make trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Yan'en urged the emperor, "Zhan and Li Xian were birds of a feather. With Xian dead, Zhan will not feel safe. Unless he is removed, he may rebel.

sentences.zh: 然展方握強兵，宜以計去之。

translations.literal: Yet Zhan just now holds a strong army—it is fitting to remove him by stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: But he still commands a strong army. He should be removed by stratagem.

sentences.zh: 請除展江淮都統，代李峘，俟其釋兵赴鎮，中道執之，此一夫力耳。」

translations.literal: I ask that Zhan be appointed overall commander of Jiang and Huai, replacing Li Kuan; wait until he releases his troops and goes to his post, seize him midway—this is only the strength of one man."
translations.idiomatic: Appoint Zhan overall commander of Jiang and Huai in Li Kuan's place, wait until he gives up his army and sets out for his post, then seize him on the road. That takes no more than one man's strength."

sentences.zh: 上從之，以展為都統淮南東、江南西、浙西三道節度使；

translations.literal: The emperor followed this; Zhan was made overall commander of the three circuits Huai South East, Jiang South West, and Zhe West;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and made Zhan overall commander of Huai South East, Jiang South West, and Zhe West;

sentences.zh: 密敕舊都統李峘及淮南東道節度使鄧景山圖之。

translations.literal: a secret edict ordered the former overall commander Li Kuan and Huai South East circuit military commissioner Deng Jingshan to plot against him.
translations.idiomatic: A secret edict ordered the former overall commander Li Kuan and Huai South East military commissioner Deng Jingshan to trap him.

sentences.zh: 延恩以制書授展，展疑之，曰：「展自陳留參軍，數年至刺史，可謂暴貴矣。

translations.literal: Yan'en gave the imperial commission to Zhan; Zhan was suspicious and said: "Zhan, from Chenliu aide, in several years reaching prefect—one may call this sudden elevation.
translations.idiomatic: Yan'en handed Zhan the imperial commission. Zhan was suspicious and said, "I rose from aide at Chenliu to prefect in only a few years—surely that is sudden favor.

sentences.zh: 江、淮租賦所出，今之重任，展無勳勞，又非親賢，一旦恩命寵擢如此，得非有讒人間之乎？」

translations.literal: Jiang and Huai are where rent and tax come from—a weighty charge today; Zhan has no meritorious toil, nor is he kin or worthy; yet suddenly gracious command favors and promotes thus—could it be that slanderers have set discord?"
translations.idiomatic: Jiang and Huai are the source of the empire's revenues—a post of grave responsibility. I have won no merit and am neither kin nor trusted counselor. To be raised so suddenly by grace—could slanderers not have set someone against me?

sentences.zh: 因泣下。

translations.literal: Thereupon he wept.
translations.idiomatic: With that he broke into tears.

sentences.zh: 延恩懼，曰：「公素有才望，主上以江、淮為憂，故不次用公。

translations.literal: Yan'en was afraid and said: "Your Lordship has long had talent and reputation; the sovereign, taking Jiang and Huai as worry, therefore used Your Lordship out of turn.
translations.idiomatic: Yan'en grew fearful and said, "Your Lordship has long enjoyed talent and renown. The sovereign is deeply troubled over Jiang and Huai and has therefore appointed you out of the usual order.

sentences.zh: 公反以為疑，何哉？」

translations.literal: Your Lordship on the contrary takes it as suspicious—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Why then do you turn it into grounds for suspicion?

sentences.zh: 展曰：「事苟不欺，印節可先得乎？」

translations.literal: Zhan said: "If the matter is truly not deceit, may the seal and staff be obtained first?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhan said, "If this is no deception, may I have the seal and staff of office first?

sentences.zh: 延恩曰：「可。」

translations.literal: Yan'en said: "It can be done."
translations.idiomatic: Yan'en said, "It can.

sentences.zh: 乃馳詣廣陵，與峘謀，解峘印節以授展。

translations.literal: Thereupon he galloped to Guangling, plotted with Kuan, removed Kuan's seal and staff and gave them to Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: He then galloped to Guangling, took counsel with Li Kuan, stripped Kuan of his seal and staff, and handed them to Zhan.

sentences.zh: 展得印節，乃上表謝恩，牒追江、淮親舊，置之心膂，三道宮屬遣使迎賀，申圖籍，相望於道，展悉舉宋州兵七千趣廣陵。

translations.literal: Zhan obtained the seal and staff, then submitted a memorial thanking grace, sent dispatches recalling Jiang-Huai kin and old associates, placed them in heart and spine; three-route palace attendants sent envoys to welcome and congratulate, presented maps and registers—one after another on the road; Zhan mustered all seven thousand Song Prefecture troops and hastened to Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhan had the seal and staff, he submitted a memorial of thanks, summoned his Jiang-Huai kinsmen and old associates, and made them his inner circle. Palace officers from three circuits sent envoys with congratulations and brought maps and registers, crowding the roads. Zhan then mustered all seven thousand troops of Song Prefecture and marched on Guangling.

sentences.zh: 延恩知展已得其情，還奔廣陵，與李峘、鄧景山發兵拒之，移檄州縣，言展反。

translations.literal: Yan'en knew Zhan had gotten the truth, returned fleeing to Guangling, with Li Kuan and Deng Jingshan raised troops to resist him, issued proclamations to prefectures and counties saying Zhan had rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Zhan had learned the truth, Yan'en fled back to Guangling. With Li Kuan and Deng Jingshan he raised troops to resist Zhan and sent proclamations through the prefectures and counties declaring that Zhan had rebelled.

sentences.zh: 展亦移檄言峘反，州縣莫知所從。

translations.literal: Zhan also issued proclamations saying Kuan had rebelled; prefectures and counties did not know whom to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan issued proclamations of his own declaring that Kuan had rebelled, and the prefectures and counties did not know whom to follow.

sentences.zh: 峘引兵渡江，與副使潤州刺史韋儇、浙西節度使侯令儀屯京口，鄧景山將萬人屯徐城。

translations.literal: Kuan led troops across the river, with deputy commissioner Run Prefecture prefect Wei Yin and Zhe West military commissioner Hou Lingyi encamped at Jingkou; Deng Jingshan led ten thousand men encamped at Xucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan led his army across the Yangzi and, with deputy commissioner and Run Prefecture prefect Wei Yin and Zhe West military commissioner Hou Lingyi, encamped at Jingkou, while Deng Jingshan stationed ten thousand men at Xucheng.

sentences.zh: 展素有威名，御軍嚴整，江、淮人望風畏之。

translations.literal: Zhan had long had a fearsome name; he commanded troops with stern order; Jiang-Huai people at sight of his wind feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan had long enjoyed a formidable reputation and kept his army under strict discipline; throughout Jiang and Huai, men feared him at the mere report of his approach.

sentences.zh: 展倍道先期至，使人問景山曰：「吾奉詔書赴鎮，此何兵也？」

translations.literal: Zhan by double marches arrived ahead of schedule, sent a man to ask Jingshan: "I, bearing the edict commission, go to my post—what army is this?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhan forced the march and arrived ahead of schedule. He sent a man to ask Jingshan, "I come by imperial edict to take up my post—what army is this?

sentences.zh: 景山不應。

translations.literal: Jingshan did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Jingshan made no reply.

sentences.zh: 展使人呼於陣前曰：「汝曹皆吾民也，勿干吾旗鼓。」

translations.literal: Zhan sent a man to shout before the battle line: "You all are my people—do not interfere with my banners and drums."
translations.idiomatic: Zhan sent a man to shout before the battle line, "You are all my people. Do not stand in the way of my banners and drums.
